hypotheses.title: Next Sort-family variant with a hybrid IAP economy (fast follow)
hypotheses.market: Game sub-genre Sort (WW; Block as secondary)
hypotheses.claim: Sort revenue is being created by new mechanics, not incumbents (entrants +$464M vs apps in both periods +$94M). A new sort/flow variant with a fresh physical metaphor (pixel fill, marble, sand, yarn, colony), built in 2-3 weeks and shipped with an IAP economy (lives, boosters, coin store, level map) on top of rewarded ads, will clear a pre-set playable-ad IPM bar against a Pixel Flow-style control and reach >= $0.50 IAP RPD in US/CA/AU, where ad-only clones of the same mechanics earn < $0.01. Falsified if all variants miss the IPM bar while the control passes, if soft-launch iOS IAP RPD by D14 is < $0.10, or if no variant passes $300K/month by month 3.

hypotheses.accessibility: High build feasibility, medium for scale: top1 Pixel Flow! 25%, top-3 44%, HHI 0.093, new entrants 76% of top-100 revenue, 45 new releases >= $1M. Hard UA: Turkey holds ~57% of the top-5 country mix, Sort is #1 in US Android game ad impressions (14.3%) and US impression share rose +5.29 pp (ad-intensity rank 10). Playable-ad throughput is the studio's edge; direct fit with the micro-game feed.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Three sort-mechanic variants (e.g. pixel-flow fill, marble pour, colony/army sort) as 20-level HTML5 builds and matching playable ads, reusing the micro-game feed engine.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Weeks 1-2: AppLovin/Unity playable-ad A/B in US/CA against a Pixel Flow-style control, killed below a pre-set IPM/CTR bar. Weeks 3-4: Android soft launch of the winner in CA/AU with remove-ads, boosters and rewarded ads, measuring D1/D7 and ARPDAU against a pre-set LTV/CPI ratio.
hypotheses.risks: Very short windows (Seat Away -86%, Bus Jam -78%; Sand Loop 0.25 and Pixel Flow! 0.57 of peak by Sep-26). CPI inflation from the impression race; clone saturation (Sort tag count 4,043 -> 6,921); clones copy within weeks. Arrow-style variants earn mostly ads. Growth may partly be re-tagging, but here it is visibly carried by named new apps. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The market numbers hold up. In niche_dynamics_game_sub_genre.csv, Sort grew from $196.9M to $753.9M (+282.8%) with H2/H1 at +62.1%. Monthly revenue is still rising: $69.5M in Jun-26, $74.3M in Jul-26, $85.5M in Aug-26 and $93.0M in Sep-26. In niche_leaders_full_game_sub_genre.csv, entrants added +$463.6M against +$94.0M from apps present in both periods. The growth is carried by named new apps, so it is not re-tagging. That the revenue is new does not make it accessible to a small studio, though. Of the $539.7M earned by top-100 apps released since 2024-10, Turkey takes $303.4M (56%) and Turkey plus France take 70%. That is the territory of scaled hybrid-casual publishers. The CSVs have no publisher names, so this is an inference from the country mix. Sort is also the #1 US Android game niche for ad impressions (14.3%, +6.9 pp), which means a UA arms race. The tag count grew from 4,043 to 6,921, yet only 14 apps released in 2026 reached the top 100, roughly 0.5% of the net additions. A few of them come from smaller hubs (Israel, Vietnam, Singapore), so entry is not impossible. The falsifier of $300K/month by month 3 equals about $3.6M a year. In the current Sort ranking that sits near rank 33 ($3.8M), around the top 0.5% of the niche, which is not reachable without real UA budget. The test plan has real gaps. Weeks 1-2 measure IPM/CTR, which are installs and clicks, not revenue. A 20-level build cannot exercise a lives/booster/coin economy, because the leaders' IAP RPD comes from long, tuned level curves (Pixel Flow! has RPD $5.50 at $185.1M). A two-week Android CA/AU soft launch will therefore show ARPDAU driven mostly by rewarded ads. The plan also contradicts its own falsifier: the falsifier is iOS IAP RPD by D14, but the soft launch is Android-only in weeks 3-4. Apps peak and fade fast: Pixel Flow! peaked in Mar-26 at $23.0M a month and Sand Loop in Mar-26, while Seat Away fell -86% and Bus Jam -78%. A 4-week test would mostly catch the start of a short lifecycle. Regulatory risk is low (no gambling, kids or AI-content exposure). The limit is measurement: arrow and Block variants are ad-monetized (Arrows Puzzle Escape: 140.5M dl, $0.7M IAP), so IAP data understates their demand, and an IAP-only bar would wrongly reject an ad-led winner.

verification.key_caveat: Sort's growth is real and comes from new apps, but about 56% of the new-release revenue goes to Turkish hybrid-casual publishers, and the UA impression race is the strongest of any game sub-genre on US Android. The proposed 4-week test measures IPM/CTR and early, mostly ad-driven ARPDAU. It cannot measure IAP RPD on a 20-level build. The $300K/month bar is about rank 33 of roughly 6,900 apps and needs UA budget. All revenue figures are App Store + Google Play IAP only; ad revenue is excluded.

verification.reasoning: I recomputed every headline number from the CSVs and all of them match within 1%. In niche_dynamics_game_sub_genre.csv, Sort has rev_cur=753,908,924.68 and rev_prior=196,945,023.96 (yoy +282.8%), rev_h2_h1=+62.1%, last3m yoy=+272.1%, RPD 0.175->0.436 and 24/24 months observed with no flags. niche_monthly also shows a smooth climb from $12.2M in Oct-24 to $93.0M in Sep-26, not a one-month launch spike. The growth does not come from reclassification. All 48 entrants into the Sort top-100 (niche_top_apps.csv, current vs prior revenue lists) were released in or after 2024-10, and none of them appears in any other niche's prior top-100. Their combined revenue is $463.55M, which matches growth_decomp_entrants_usd exactly. The "both periods" bucket (+$94.0M) also includes recent launches such as Gecko Out (2025-01, $2.7M->$29.9M), so "incumbents" overstates its age. The trend is not one app either: top1 Pixel Flow! has a 25.0% share and HHI is 0.093. Growth is still hit-driven, though. Pixel Flow! alone is about 33% of the +$557M revenue increase, and the top-5 entrants are about 54%. The H2 lift is carried by a rolling relay of hits: Pixel Flow! peaked in Mar-26 at $23.0M/month, while Colony Flow!, Jelly Busters and Food Hunt each peaked in Sep-26. That supports the claim about short windows. The main data caveats concern the revenue-test thresholds, not the market trend. First, US = $463.5M of the $754M (61%), with niche RPD US $2.06, CA $1.14, AU $1.91, so the trend is essentially a US iOS-heavy IAP phenomenon (Pixel Flow! iOS share 66.5%). Second, the entrant RPD of $0.83 is computed only on survivors in the top-100. Third, the claim that ad-only clones earn under $0.01 measures IAP RPD only: Arrows Puzzle Escape's ad revenue is invisible to Sensor Tower, so it says nothing about their total RPD. The "casual median 4 months to $1M" figure relies on raw JSON outside the data room, so I could not reproduce it.

verification.key_caveat: Sort's +283% is real: it is carried by named new releases, not re-tagging. But it is a hit relay: Pixel Flow! alone is about 33% of the growth, and the top-5 entrants about 54%. It is also US-iOS-heavy IAP (the US is 61% of revenue). hypotheses.title: Ad-monetized arrow-escape / logic puzzles riding a short download wave
hypotheses.market: Sort / Maze / Riddle download-led puzzles (WW; cheapest validation in IN/PK/ID and BR/PH)
hypotheses.claim: Sort's download growth (+600.7M) is carried largely by near-zero-IAP arrow-escape titles (Arrows Puzzle Escape, Arrows GO!, Arrow Puzzle = 321.1M downloads, ~$0.79M IAP). An arrow/logic puzzle entered before the next download peak can reach tens of millions of installs within one ~3-month cycle and pay back through ads. Falsified if arrow playables do not beat the Sort control on CPI/IPM, or if a 3-week test gives 30-day ad LTV/CPI < 0.7 (target >= 1.0).

hypotheses.accessibility: Very high to build (days to weeks) and to buy installs (IN country RPD $0.034; IN/PK/ID Sort downloads +65% / +70% / +87%). Store revenue is not the business model here, so economics must be measured from ad mediation. Intense cloning (22 arrow titles already in the Maze top-100, 43 arrow-titled releases since 2025-07).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Three arrow-escape playable variants (classic, color-gated, timed), plus the same levels as a feed card with rewarded continue.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Android launch in 2-3 Tier-2/3 markets (e.g. BR, ID, PH) with $2-3K UA. Measure CPI, D1/D7 and ad ARPDAU from mediation over 3 weeks. Pass if 30-day LTV/CPI >= 1.0.
hypotheses.risks: size_cur_usd is the Sort niche IAP total used by two analysts; the arrow wave itself earns only ~$1.2M IAP (43 titles, 348.9M dl), so the dollar size is a demand proxy, not the opportunity's revenue. Trend window is short (Arrows Puzzle Escape monthly downloads fell ~87% in 4 months). Low eCPMs in IN/PK; policy risk on ad density; taxonomy split across Sort/Maze/Riddle. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android. Ad revenue cannot be verified with this data. Confidence conflict across analysts (crosscheck-01 0.6, entrants-03 0.5, countries-07 0.4): set to the mean 0.5 instead of the max 0.6.

verification.reasoning: Building an arrow puzzle is easy, but getting a hit in this wave is not. Payoffs are winner-take-most. 47 arrow-titled games released since 2025-07 sit in the sub-genre top-100s with 350.9M downloads and $1.22M IAP between them. The top three alone have 321.1M of those downloads (92%): Arrows Puzzle Escape (Germany, 140.5M), Arrows GO! (China, 99.0M) and Arrow Puzzle: Tap (Cyprus, 81.6M). Only 3 of the 47 passed 10M downloads and 10 passed 1M. The 22 arrow titles released since 2026-04, which is the realistic position of a new entrant, peak at 7.8M (Cash Arrows), and most have under 1M. So the claim that a title can reach "tens of millions of installs within one cycle" holds for the first movers, not for an entrant arriving after the May-2026 peak. Sort's $753.9M IAP figure says nothing about this opportunity. The niche's revenue growth comes from IAP hybrid-casual entrants (entrants = 85% of the absolute revenue change; Pixel Flow! alone is $185.1M = 25% of the top-100; Turkey holds 56.6% of top-100 revenue), and the US provides $463.5M of it. The arrow titles earn almost nothing in-store. Sort downloads held at about 182M/month from Jul to Sep 2026 even as the lead arrow title collapsed, so download demand rotates between formats rather than staying with arrows. The proposed test has two problems. First, the CPI/IPM comparison of playables measures clicks, not revenue. Second, a 3-week run cannot observe 30-day ad LTV; it can only project it from D7 ARPDAU. It also runs in markets where store monetization per download is tiny (country RPD IN $0.035, PK $0.014, ID $0.091, PH $0.146, BR $0.207), so eCPMs are likely low too. None of the ad economics can be checked with this data. The test is feasible and does measure money if mediation ARPDAU is used, but the falsification rule needs to say that the 30-day figure is projected, and the hypothesis should be reframed as "be first on the next format rotation" rather than "ride the arrow wave".

verification.key_caveat: The $753.9M Sort figure is in-store IAP, earned mostly by Turkish hybrid-casual IAP titles and 61% from the US. The arrow wave itself earned about $1.2M IAP, and ad revenue cannot be seen in this data at all (store IAP and paid downloads only). Of the 22 arrow titles released after 2026-04, none passed 8M downloads, so a late entrant should expect a small outcome.

verification.reasoning:
The raw numbers reproduce to within 1%. Sort (niche_dynamics_game_sub_genre.csv) went from $196.9M to $753.9M (+282.8%), and its downloads from 1,127.2M to 1,727.9M (+600.7M, +53.3%; last3m +112.8%). The arrow trio in niche_top_apps.csv (Sort, current, downloads ranks 1/2/4) totals 140.53M + 99.01M + 81.60M = 321.1M dl with $0.786M IAP. Net of Arrows Puzzle Escape's 0.82M prior downloads (leaders.csv), the trio adds +320.3M, which is 53.3% of the delta. The US impression shift of +5.29 pp is in fact the largest of any game sub-genre. The IN/PK/ID download figures and the 45.6M / 31.0M / 26.1M IN arrow entrants also match.

Three things weaken the claim:
1. The dollar size is a different market. Sort IAP growth is 85% entrants (niche_leaders_full growth_decomp_entrants_share=0.851). It comes from IAP hits: Pixel Flow! $185.1M (top1_share 0.25), Magic Sort! $94.8M and Yarn Loop $43.2M. The arrow trio is about 0.1% of Sort IAP, so size_cur_usd=$753.9M says nothing about this opportunity.
2. "Tens of millions within one cycle" rests on survivors. Of 44 puzzle-genre arrow titles released since 2025-07 that appear in any per-niche top-100, only 3 passed 10M dl and only 10 passed 1M. The median is 0.23M. The top 3 hold 92% of the 350.0M arrow downloads.
3. The taxonomy is split. Arrow titles are tagged Sort (6), Maze (22) and Riddle (6). The Sort tag count grew from 4,043 to 6,921 and Maze from 1,267 to 3,388, so "Sort download growth" is partly an artifact of where Sensor Tower files each clone.

At niche level the wave has not reversed. Monthly Sort downloads stepped up from 121.0M (Mar-26) to 168.7–188.2M (Apr–Sep-26) and stayed there. The per-app decline of Arrows Puzzle Escape (29.8M to 3.8M) comes from raw series that are not in out/ and cannot be verified here.

The IN Sort revenue PI computes to 0.34 (0.004555/0.013396), not 0.29. IN RPD of $0.035 is store revenue per download, not CPI, so it does not show that installs are cheap. Ad LTV, the actual business model, is invisible in this data.

The theme hook can be tested before content is built: a themed merge board with an episodic short-drama hook beats a plain-merge control on playable-ad CTR/IPM, store-page conversion and in-feed 'unlock next episode' intent. Falsified if themed creatives do not beat merge benchmarks, or the merge-story playable's IPM is < 50% of a match-pair control.

hypotheses.risks: Test-design hypothesis, not a market: the size used for ranking is the hybridcasual product-model pool it would be applied to ($3,309M), not money it earns by itself (monetization analyst cited the whole device total, $40.5B). Evidence rests on a handful of apps; China Android absence inflates iOS shares (excluded by the analyst). Small cohorts give noisy RPD; SKAN delays iOS reads. Android matters more for ad-monetized variants. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: This is a test method, not a market. Its key evidence does not hold up once you look inside casual puzzle. Across Sort, Block, Screw, Eat & Grow and Match Pair in leaders.csv, the revenue-weighted iOS share is 0.689 for entrants and 0.678 for incumbents, so entrants are not more iOS-skewed. In Sort, the largest niche, the gap runs the other way: entrants 0.645 vs incumbents 0.723. The Block Out! split ($48.8M, s_ios_rev_share_cur=0.9999, only 1.0M Android downloads) shows a publisher that barely launched on Android. It tells us nothing about how Android users monetize. The device data also cuts against an iOS-only go/no-go: Android IAP grew +12.1% and iPhone +5.5% (niche_dynamics_device.csv). In Sort, US ad-impression share on Android is 14.3% (+6.9pp) vs 7.4% on iOS, and the niche ranks 10th for ad intensity. That suggests a large part of Android value is ad revenue, which IAP data cannot see. So a test that compares only IAP RPD will undercount Android. The falsification rule is close to automatic: global Android/iPhone RPD is 0.356/2.27 ≈ 16%, far below the 70% threshold. The test therefore confirms the prior, while D7/D14 IAP from small CA/AU cohorts over 3 weeks is noisy and slowed by SKAN reporting delays. The rule also conflicts with the prototype, which says 'Android behind a feature flag', because a parallel soft launch of the same build needs a full Android build. On access: Sort/Block entrants take a large share (Sort new-entrant share 0.763, 48 entrants into the top 100), but the winners are scaled hybridcasual publishers. Turkey has 56.6% of the Sort top 5 and 80.8% of Block. Block's top 3 hold 77%, and Screwdom alone holds 45% of Screw. Hybridcasual revenue rose +24% while downloads fell -12.3%, so the gains come from monetizing existing players harder, not from new audience. As a cost-saving launch method the idea is plausible and low-risk, with no gambling or kids-specific regulatory flags. As evidence of a revenue opportunity it is not established.

hypotheses.prototype_idea: Feed of 30-60 s story scenes, each ending in a one-tap mini-game (merge or sort) that changes the AI character's reply; weekly subscription for unlimited chat and episodes.

verification.reasoning: The market numbers reproduce exactly from niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv (AI Companion row). Top-100 revenue went from $170.69M to $473.83M (+177.6%), with top1 Tipsy Chat at 11.5%, top3 at 29.4%, HHI 0.0441 and new_entrants_share 0.493. Generative AI ($2,642M to $6,320M, +139.2%, H2/H1 +46.8%, US ad-intensity rank 28) and Interactive Story (-25.9%; -16.3% without Love and Deepspace) also check out. The label "entrant-driven" does not survive the growth decomposition. Of the +$303.1M delta, the 61 apps present in both periods' top-100 add +$215.0M (71%) and the 39 entrants add only +$108.1M (36%). Two of those both-period apps, Tipsy Chat (+$53.8M from $0.69M) and zeta (+$44.0M from $3.72M), account for 32% of the delta. The 49% "new entrants" share counts apps by recent release date (Tipsy, released 2024-08, counts as one), not apps new to the top-100. Tipsy is also a late spike rather than a steady trend: H2/H1 +778%, and September 2026 ($17.8M) alone is about a third of its 12-month revenue. Even so, the niche is still +123% without the top-2 apps ($371.5M vs $166.3M), so the growth is broad rather than one hit, and the AI Companion filter applies today's tags to both periods, so reclassification inflating the YoY is unlikely. The claim that AI Companion is "absorbing spend from Interactive Story" has no support in the data. $128.5M of the Interactive Story drop ($379.9M to $251.4M) comes from one 3D otome game, Love and Deepspace. Interactive Story publishers are 70.9% Chinese, while AI Companion publishers are 44% US and 20% Korean. Only one app, キャラぷ ($11.6M), carries both tags. The two series simply moved at the same time; nothing here shows users moving between them. verification.reasoning: The market part holds up. In niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv, the AI Companion top-100 grew from $170.7M to $473.8M (+177.6%), with HHI 0.044, top-1 at 11.5% and top-3 at 29.4%. The #100 app earns only $0.68M. Apps present in both periods account for 70.9% of the growth ($215.0M: zeta, PolyBuzz, CHAI); entrants add only $108.1M (35.7%). The 49.3% "new entrant" share counts releases back to 2024-08. The CAC < $30 gate is also inconsistent with the niche: the top-100's revenue per download is $2.31 (only Tipsy reaches about $10). hypotheses.title: Monetize the micro-game feed as a hybrid: rewarded unlocks + coin packs + pass
hypotheses.market: Hybridcasual product model; Mini-game Hub + Riddle download pools; Short Drama as the feed analogue
hypotheses.claim: Casual IAP per install is deepening (hybridcasual $2,661M -> $3,309M, RPD $0.40 -> $0.57) while feed-native entertainment shows ad-supported free tiers capturing download growth as IAP RPD falls (Movies & TV dl +33.8% vs rev +5.9%). The studio's micro-game feed therefore monetizes best as a hybrid: free plays, rewarded ads for extra tries, coin packs and an optional no-ads/booster pass with a cross-game collection meta. Falsified if a paywall-only arm beats hybrid on IAP+ad revenue per install, if the pass fake door converts < 0.3% of D7 actives, or if the IAP layer cuts session length vs control.

evidence.metric: Movies & TV Shows revenue vs downloads

evidence.value: $1,840.9M->$2,241.4M (+21.8%); RPD 1.57->1.38; downloads of apps in both periods +19.3%

hypotheses.accessibility: High: reuses existing feed infrastructure, no new market entry. As a stand-alone 'offline mini-games' app, Mini-game Hub is fragmented (top1 25%, HHI 0.148) but its IAP pool is tiny (< $50M) and its value is ad revenue (831M top-100 downloads, top-20 RPD $0.003).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Feed-level 'Pass' (no ads, daily boosters, exclusive skins) plus a cross-game collection meta.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 3-week 2-arm A/B (hybrid vs paywall) on a CA/AU soft-launch cohort of ~5k installs per arm; compare IAP + ad revenue per install.
hypotheses.risks: Feed users may be ad-tolerant but IAP-averse; the macro trend does not guarantee feed-level conversion; the short-drama analogy may not transfer to games; kids/offline traffic is low-intent. Size is the hybridcasual pool used as context, not addressable revenue. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The macro numbers check out. Hybridcasual made $3,309.1M vs $2,661.4M (+24.3%), last3m +38.0%, and quarterly revenue went from $598.0M (Q4-2024) to $957.4M (Q3-2026). But that growth is IAP per install deepening at incumbents, not demand a newcomer can reach: Hybridcasual downloads fell -12.3% (6,605M to 5,794M) and Hypercasual art-style downloads fell -22.2% while its RPD doubled. That looks like existing ad-monetized catalogs bolting on IAP, or a re-tag from hypercasual to hybrid. The product-model dimension has no leader or concentration table, so neither new-entrant access nor reclassification can be ruled out. The feed analogues push against a stand-alone entry. Short Drama is incumbent and UA-scaled: DramaBox $391.2M, top3 44.9%, and Singapore, Hong Kong and China publishers hold about 64% of the top-5 mix. Mini-game Hub's whole top-100 IAP pool is $11.0M, and new entrants hold only 5.6% of it. Riddle is the one accessible pool (new entrants 76.0% of top-100, entrants explain 109.5% of growth), but it is $23.0M and Turkey-dominated (51.3%). Because Sensor Tower counts no ad revenue, the "ad-supported free tier wins" part (FreeReels 283.2M dl / $0.2M IAP) cannot be checked on revenue at all: it is a download fact, not a monetization fact. The proposed test is the bigger problem. With 5k installs per arm and about 15-20% D7 retention, the 0.3% pass fake-door threshold means roughly 2-3 clicks per arm. That measures intent clicks, not revenue, and it is statistically noise. With casual payer rates around 1-2%, a 3-week IAP+ad revenue-per-install comparison can only detect differences of about 50% or more. Platform risk: the studio's feed is Telegram-first, so a pass and coin packs there run on Stars/Telegram rules, not on the store economics in this data. Kids-skewed hub traffic (Budge Kids Games 2-7 is the #1 hub) brings COPPA and Families-policy limits on ads and IAP. An auto-renew pass also brings subscription-disclosure rules.

verification.reasoning: I re-derived every headline number and all of them hold within rounding. Hybridcasual product model: rev $3,309.1M vs $2,661.4M (+24.3%), last3m +37.95%, RPD $0.403 to $0.571, and Q4-2024 $598.0M to Q3-2026 $957.4M. That actually fits the 'free/ad tier captures downloads' mechanism, but it means incumbent IAP is not eroding. Riddle's +96% IAP growth comes entirely from new releases: entrants contributed +$12.1M while apps present in both periods fell $0.68M. Mini-game Hub is similar: $9.6M to $11.2M, top1 Budge 25%, HHI 0.148. Above all, Sensor Tower measures IAP only, so nothing in the data room can show that hybrid beats paywall on IAP plus ads. verification.reasoning: The data contradicts the hypothesis's main claim of "unmet demand" for an ad-monetized drama format in SEA. The download surge in the Short Drama category comes from free, ad-funded apps that scaled publishers already run. In PH, FreeReels is the #1 download (28.8M dl, $0.01M IAP) and Melolo has 14.3M dl and $0.20M IAP. In ID, Melolo is #1 (100.3M dl, $2.62M IAP), FreeReels is #2 (80.9M dl) and PineDrama, a China-published app released in 2025-12, is #8 (52.5M dl, about $0 IAP). The "downloads outrun IAP" gap also shrinks once you measure Short Drama itself instead of the whole Movies & TV Shows category. Short Drama apps in the PH top-300 revenue list grew IAP from $22.2M to $31.5M (+42%); in ID they went from $39.4M to $40.9M (+3.8%). The PH Movies & TV category also has positive H2/H1 momentum (+17.9%). Worldwide, Short Drama IAP growth goes mostly to existing players. Apps present in both periods account for 77% of the change, while the 43 entrants into the top-100 earned only $148.3M, 6.6% of $2,241M. The 38.6% "new-entrant share" mostly belongs to well-funded 2024 launches: NetShort ($248.3M, SG) and Dramawave ($227.4M, US). Concentration is high: top-3 hold 44.9% and top-10 hold 76.4%. The revenue test itself is sound because ad ARPDAU plus unlock conversion measures money, not clicks. But four weeks is tight once you add producing and localizing enough 60-second episodes to measure D7, and soft-launch traffic must be bought against FreeReels/Melolo-scale UA in a low-eCPM market. ($185.1M), Marble Sort! ($31.0M), Sand Loop ($21.9M). hypotheses.title: AI-produced interactive micro-drama with mini-game cliffhangers
hypotheses.market: App IQ leaf Short Drama (Movies & TV Shows)
hypotheses.claim: Short drama is entrant-driven (top-100 $1,841M -> $2,241M, new entrants 38.6%, HHI 0.09) and AI production has already produced a fast new label (VibeShort: AI Short Dramas, $35.5M, released 2026-02, 1 month to $1M/month). AI-made episodes with a mini-game choice at each cliffhanger can monetize per viewer comparably to live-action: at least 2% of viewers pay to unlock on a web test. Falsified if unlock conversion is < 2% or < 50% of the live-action benchmark.

evidence.value: NetShort $248.3M (+120%), Dramawave $227.4M; VibeShort: AI Short Dramas $35.5M (rel 2026-02)
$35.5M, 1 month to $1M/mo, at peak in Sep-26
39% new releases; 17 new >= $5M; StoryReel $27.5M within 5 months

hypotheses.accessibility: Low-medium: unconcentrated but a UA arms race (SG/US/HK publishers ~87% of the country mix); incumbents fatigue (ReelShort -8%, ShortMax -30%). The small-team angle is AI production cost plus interactivity, and the vertical-feed UX is native to a micro-game feed studio.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: 10-episode AI romance micro-drama, 60 s episodes, a 15 s mini-game picks the branch at each cliffhanger; coins unlock episodes 4+.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Produce 3 episodes in 2 weeks; in-feed ads to a web player with coin unlock, US + PH, $3k. Pass: episode-1 completion ≥ 60%, unlock ≥ 2%, CAC per payer ≤ week-1 revenue per payer.
hypotheses.risks: AI video quality; store review and policy for AI-generated media; incumbent UA spend; flat US attention (Movies & TV US time -2%). Web unlock revenue is outside this data. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning:
The niche is real and growing: the Short Drama top-100 rose from $1,841M to $2,241M (+21.8%). It is not "entrant-driven" in a way that helps a small team, though. The growth decomposition puts 77% of the gross change on apps present in both periods ($308M), against $148M (37%) from the 43 apps that entered the top-100. The 38.6% "new entrant" share is mostly NetShort ($248.3M) and Dramawave ($227.4M), released in mid-2024 and run by scale publishers in Singapore and the US. HHI of 0.09 hides a heavy head: the top 3 take 44.9% and the top 10 take 76.4%.

The AI proof point (VibeShort) also points against accessibility. VibeShort ($35.5M, 33.6M dl) and StoryReel ($27.5M, 30.9M dl) are both from Hong Kong publishers. Together they hold 60% of the $104.9M earned by the 22 top-100 apps released since 2025-10, and that download scale means incumbent-level UA. The other 20 new releases earn about $0.8–6.2M each. Hong Kong, Singapore and the US make up 87% of top-100 revenue, and rank #100 earns only $0.77M a year.

The revenue test as designed does not work. The prototype paywalls episodes 4+, but only 3 episodes would be produced, so the "unlock" becomes a fake-door click rather than a real payment. A real web coin purchase needs a payment stack, which is a money/payment act in the operator's own process. The "50% of live-action benchmark" criterion has no source: Sensor Tower provides no conversion rates, and web unlock revenue is outside this data. Spread across US and PH, $3k buys roughly 1–3k landings, so 2% means only 20–60 payers, and nothing isolates the effect of the mini-game choice.

Other headwinds:
- Movies & TV US time-spent fell 2.2% and revenue per download fell from $2.07 to $1.64, while downloads grew 34%.
- FreeReels shows the ad-monetized model (283.2M dl, $0.16M IAP), so part of the demand is invisible in IAP, and that slice is dominated by distribution scale rather than studio craft.
- Risks include AI-content disclosure under store and ad-network policy, and web-subscription/negative-option rules.
- Fit with a puzzle/merge studio is weak: the scarce skill here is serialized video plus UA, not mechanics.

"At least 3 requests for a briefed creative" is an interest signal, not revenue, and only "at least 1 paid pilot" counts. Four weeks is also short for vendor onboarding and procurement at Chinese SLG publishers, most of which run in-house creative teams or cheap Chinese outsourcing. Platform and regulatory risk is low; the main risks are price pressure and IP or ad-claim compliance, such as fake-gameplay ads.

hypotheses.title: Personalized AI song/meme gift product
hypotheses.market: AI Content Generator leaf + AI music apps tagged elsewhere
hypotheses.claim: AI music creation is new-app-driven. A per-song 'song for a person' gift can reach at least 3% landing-to-checkout from paid social. Falsified if under 1.5%.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium-high: HHI 0.09 (Suno 26% of top 100); runs on third-party/open models; viral share loop fits the team.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Name + occasion + 3 facts gives a 30 s song with a lyric video and share link; $3.99 per song, $9.99 for a 3-pack, 'make one back' loop.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Web landing plus $2k TikTok/Meta for 2 weeks around a gifting date with a real web checkout. Pass: checkout ≥ 3%, ≥ 0.3 shares per buyer.
hypotheses.risks: Licensing and copyright, per-song cost, fad decay (Mozart H2/H1 -23%), web revenue outside the benchmark data. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers check out. The AI Content Generator row in niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv shows top-100 revenue of $354.87M vs $197.84M (+79.4%), new-entrant share 0.585, HHI 0.093 and Suno top1 = $91.9M. A tight regex over niche_top_apps.csv (app_iq_category, revenue order) finds 39 AI song/music apps across 9 leaves: $186.2M vs $57.4M (+224%), with 68% from apps released on or after 2024-07, and $46.1M sits in Musical Instrument Apps (the claim says $48.2M). The mechanism "new-app-driven" does not hold up. The niche's own growth decomposition credits $139.7M (89% of the absolute change) to apps that were in the top 100 in both periods, only $33.7M to entrants and -$16.4M to exits. The "58.5% new" figure is a release-date cut (on or after 2024-07), not churn. The growth is also one hit. Suno adds $74.7M of the niche's $157.0M net gain (48%) and makes up 49% of the music cluster, and Suno, Kling and Jimeng together add about $117M (75%). Without Suno the cluster is $94.3M vs $40.2M (+135%), and only about 38% of that comes from apps released on or after 2024-07. The gift-style song generators a small team would copy have lost momentum (leaders.csv s_rev_h2_h1): MyTunes -6.4%, Donna +2.2%, Mozart -23.4%, Rythmix -6.7%. Only Suno (+61.6%, peak month 2026-09) and Sondo, a newer music-video app (2025-04), are accelerating. The tag count grew only 4125 to 4719, so reclassification is a minor factor. The niche row also has no ww_total value, so top-100 coverage of the whole tag is unknown. The 3% / 1.5% landing-to-checkout threshold cannot be checked in this data at all, because Sensor Tower has no web/D2C payments, paid-social funnels or per-song gift purchases.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers check out. AI Content Generator top-100 is $354.9M vs $197.8M (+79.4%), with new-entrant share 58.5% and HHI 0.093. The AI-music cluster, rebuilt as 42 regex-matched apps, is $187.4M vs $61.3M (+206%), and 67.7% of it comes from apps released 2024-07 or later. But "new-app-driven" does not mean open to new entrants. In the niche's growth decomposition, 89% of the absolute change came from apps already in the top-100 in both periods. The 35 apps that entered the top-100 added only $33.7M in total, about $1M each. The niche's top 3 are Suno, Kling (Kuaishou) and Jimeng (ByteDance), holding 42.7% of the top-100. Suno, which owns its model, has all the momentum: H2/H1 +62%, last3m +296%, peak month 2026-09. The wrapper apps a small team would be competing with have stalled: MyTunes H2/H1 -6%, Mozart -23%, Rythmix -7%, Donna +2%. The nine apps released in 2025 or later earn only $15.9M combined, and most of that is music-video variants (Sondo $6.1M). Publisher mix is US 53% (mostly Suno) and Turkey 25%, i.e. established wrapper studios that already run heavy paid UA. So a wrapper can win a few $1-10M slots, but the category's growth is going to a model owner and a few big platforms, not to newcomers. The test does measure revenue, because it uses a real checkout. It is also feasible in 4 weeks with a third-party music API and $2k: roughly 1.5-4k visits is enough to tell 3% from 1.5%. Its weakness is economics. The pass bar has no CAC or ROAS check: at a $1 CPC and 3% conversion, cost per buyer is about $33 against $3.99-9.99 per order, so a "pass" can still lose money. The store evidence is subscription creation tools sold in-app, while the test is a one-off web gift purchase that Sensor Tower does not cover, so the data says little about this exact product. There are also copyright and voice-likeness risks (label litigation against AI music firms, and Suno has no official public API), plus AI-content ad-policy risk. The fit with a casual puzzle, merge and playable-ads team is weak.

hypotheses.title: India: the fastest-growing large IAP market, best used as a low-CPI monetization test bed
hypotheses.market: IN (all apps/games)
hypotheses.claim: India's IAP growth (Codex public +34% H1-26) is real and broad-based (apps, GenAI, short drama). Low-price passes in India will convert at a payer rate per 1k installs comparable to BR, at lower CPI.

evidence.value: Utilities +$44.2M, Generative AI +$39.5M (+150%), Movies & TV +$30.7M, Social +$26.6M; Match Swap +$7.8M (+36.8%, base $21.1M)

evidence.metric: Local publisher share / games share of top-300

hypotheses.accessibility: High for testing (cheap installs; foreign publishers dominate, local share 7.8%). Low for revenue scale (0.7% of WW).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: An India arm of the micro-game feed with an INR 29-49 weekly pass and an ad-removal SKU.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 4-week A/B: India vs Brazil cohorts at equal spend; compare CPI, payer conversion per 1k installs and ARPPU.
hypotheses.risks: Low ARPPU. Payments friction (UPI vs store billing). India revenue too small to justify a dedicated product. Ties to the feed-monetization hypothesis (India arm of the feed). Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce exactly from country_dynamics.csv. IN revenue went $688.2M -> $905.2M (+31.5%), last3m +32.2%, H2/H1 +17.3%, dl +3.8%. It is the fastest of 21 markets with prior revenue above $500M (MX +29.3%, TR +24.3%). The niche deltas in country_niche_dynamics.csv also reproduce: Utilities +$44.2M, GenAI +$39.5M (+150%), Movies & TV +$30.7M, Social +$26.6M, Match Swap +$7.78M (+36.8% on $21.1M). Two claims do not survive the check. (1) "Broad-based": the growth is almost entirely in apps. App sub-categories grew $421.4M -> $604.8M (+43.5%), while game sub-genres grew only $267.9M -> $297.5M (+11.1%, about +$29.6M, roughly 14% of the $216.9M delta). The app growth is concentrated in a few global subscription apps. In the India top-300 (country_leaders.csv), Google One alone added +$30.1M ($50.6M -> $80.8M), about 14% of the whole delta and probably most of the Utilities line. ChatGPT (+$13.5M), Claude (+$13.5M) and Grok (+$3.5M) together explain about 77% of the GenAI +$39.5M. Short drama is visible in downloads (Story TV 136.7M dl, Kuku TV 93.3M) but only about $3-4M per app in revenue. (2) "Payer conversion per 1k installs comparable to BR" has no support in the data, and the data points the other way. No payer-rate field exists. Revenue per download is $0.035 in IN against $0.207 in BR (rpd_cur_usd), so IAP revenue per 1k installs is about $35 vs $207, roughly six times lower. Games are 35.0% of the IN top-300, and Battle Royale (Free Fire $78.6M, BGMI $32.5M) is 15.1% of it, so casual-puzzle IAP in India is a small pool (Match Swap $28.9M, Match Merge 2 $9.6M). Growth looks organic rather than a taxonomy artifact, since the same incumbents grew and every top contributor sits in both periods' lists. The measurement boundary still matters: store IAP only, so India's large UPI/D2C web payments and ad revenue are invisible, and shifts between store billing and alternative billing could move these numbers.

verification.reasoning: The headline growth is real: India grew from $688.2M to $905.2M (+31.5%), last3m is +32.2% and H2/H1 is +17.3% (country_dynamics.csv). It is not broad-based, though, and a new entrant cannot easily get at it. In India's top-300 by revenue, the overall gain was +$176.2M. Seven US incumbents produced 50% of it: Google One +$30.2M, ChatGPT +$13.5M, Claude +$13.4M, Crunchyroll +$9.3M, Instagram +$8.5M, Facebook +$7.8M and YouTube +$5.3M. Games added only +$21.8M of that gain (country_leaders.csv), and game sub-genres in total grew just $267.9M→$297.5M (+11%), against +43.5% for app sub-categories (country_niche_dynamics.csv). The central testable claim is that payer conversion will be comparable to Brazil. The data points the other way. Revenue per download is $0.035 in India vs $0.207 in Brazil (6.0x lower). Within the studio's own genres the gap is the same: Match Swap earns $0.28/dl in India vs $1.81 in Brazil, and Sort earns $0.005/dl ($1.36M on 282M downloads) vs $0.054 in Brazil. So India's casual-puzzle demand is overwhelmingly ad-monetized, which store-IAP data cannot see. Any 4-week A/B would mostly measure India's low ARPPU (average revenue per paying user), not a margin over Brazil. The test itself is feasible and does measure revenue (payers per 1k installs, ARPPU), so the plan is not refuted. But the result would not carry over to Western markets, and the payoff is capped at 0.7% of worldwide IAP. Even the puzzle/merge gains in India went to incumbents: Candy Crush +$1.8M, Gardenscapes +$1.9M, Tasty Travels +$2.7M and Royal Kingdom +$1.3M. Regulatory note: India's 2025 online-gaming law bans real-money gaming. Any pass/loot or chance-based SKU must avoid looking like gambling (e.g. Teen Patti/rummy-style apps among local publishers), and store billing vs UPI friction will push down measured conversion.

hypotheses.title: AI speaking tutor built as role-play micro-games
hypotheses.market: Language Education leaf
hypotheses.claim: Growth outside Duolingo comes from AI speaking tutors. A role-play speaking game can match their install-to-trial conversion. Falsified if D1 is under 30% or trial under 5% in a one-country soft launch.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium: $371M outside the top 3, new-entrant share 8.3%; spoken-English demand in emerging markets (English Seekho 27.9M dl).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: 10 voice role-play scenes (interview, cafe, airport) as 2-minute mini-games with an AI partner, star ratings and a skill map; weekly subscription.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 3-week build; soft launch in one country plus a US iOS cohort, $3k TikTok. Pass: D1 ≥ 30%, trial ≥ 6%, US cost per trial ≤ $8.
hypotheses.risks: Duolingo copying the feature; voice-LLM cost; low emerging-market ARPU; UA-subsidized competitors. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The niche numbers check out ($1,179.8M vs $1,004.3M, +17.5%; Duolingo top1_share 0.592, HHI 0.358). The claim that "growth outside Duolingo comes from AI speaking tutors" holds in direction, but the growth is concentrated rather than spread across new teams. I summed the revenue change across the 119 apps that appear in the current or prior top-100 (niche_top_apps.csv): it totals +$175.5M. Duolingo alone added +$80.6M (46%), and one UAE app, Learna AI, added +$48.6M (28%). Learna earns only $0.98 per download on 64.2M downloads, which suggests heavy paid user acquisition. Apps entering the top-100 brought in only $21.1M across 19 entrants (growth_decomp_entrants_usd), and the bar to enter the top-100 is about $0.56M. AI-named apps excluding Learna went from $33.8M to $78.1M, but most of that is established tutors: Praktika ($23.0M, released 2022) and Loora ($19.3M, released 2021). Fewer than a dozen apps released since 2024 earn $1.5–6.4M each. Accessibility to a new entrant is also undercut by a 2025–26 flood of near-identical AI tutors from Vietnam, India and Turkey. They reach 1–10M downloads with roughly $0 store revenue (Linguza 8.8M, Langla 7.4M, Fluzy 10.6M downloads), so cheap installs do not turn into store revenue. Indian spoken-English apps with large download counts (English Seekho 27.9M, Supernova 22.4M) show about $0 store revenue. They most likely take payments on the web or outside the stores, so demand in emerging markets cannot be priced from this data. The proposed test mostly measures intent, not revenue. D1 and trial-start rate are top-of-funnel signals, and 3 weeks with $3k on TikTok (about 375 trials at $8 per trial) cannot observe trial-to-paid conversion, refunds or weekly renewal. Per-minute voice-LLM costs also stay unmeasured. The fit with a micro-game studio is real (role-play scenes as mini-games) and a build is feasible within 4 weeks. Still, the hypothesis should only pass if a paid-conversion metric is added.

hypotheses.title: Hard-paywall utility with a swipe-game UX (phone/photo cleaner)
hypotheses.market: Utilities ex Google One; File Management, QR, TV-remote, 2FA leaves
hypotheses.claim: Single-purpose iOS weekly-subscription utilities still let new entrants into the top 100. A swipe-game cleaner can recover CPI within 60 days. Falsified if CPI divided by install-to-paid exceeds 60-day ARPPU in a 4-week US test.
hypotheses.accessibility: Easy to build (2 weeks); medium to win: HHI 0.05-0.11, but a UA arms race. Swipe-feed UX and playable ads are a direct edge.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: 'Swipe Clean': photo cleaner as a game (swipe keep/delete, combos, daily storage goal, duplicate-merge); $6.99/week or $29.99/year after the first 100 swipes.
hypotheses.revenue_test: App Store launch; $4k on Apple Search Ads plus AppLovin playable, US, 2 weeks. Pass: CPI ≤ $2.5, trial ≥ 10%, trial-to-paid ≥ 25%.
hypotheses.risks: App Review action on deceptive subscriptions, refunds, rising CPI, native OS cleaners, low retention. Size is the File Management leaf top-100; Utilities sub-category is $6,702M. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: Every headline number reproduces within 1%, but the CSVs do not support how the hypothesis reads them. 1) The Utilities "+34%" is mostly one app. Google One is $3,362M of the $6,702M and made about 68% of the $1,691M gain; without it the sub-category grew +19.4%. 2) File Management top-100 grew +$134.4M (+35.9%). Cleanup alone added +$63.2M (47%), and WeTransfer, a file-transfer app rather than a cleaner, added +$31.8M (24%). Without both, the niche grew +14.2%. All cleaner-named apps except Cleanup grew only +12.2% YoY. 3) The cleaner segment is losing momentum. Across the 12 cleaner apps other than Cleanup in leaders.csv, H2 revenue was 11.6% below H1, and most of them fell over the last 3 months year on year: Cleaner Guru -32%, AI Cleaner -15%, Cleanup App -39%, and the 2024 entrant "Cleaner: Photo Cleanup" -73%. Swipewipe, the direct swipe-UX comparable, is flat (H2/H1 +2%, last3m -6.5%). 4) The "new-entrant share" figures count apps released since about mid-2024, so they include 15-27-month-old apps. For QR they also include Olive, an AI weight-loss app tagged as a QR scanner ($4.4M, about 12% of QR new-entrant revenue), which is a taxonomy artifact. Revenue from apps that actually entered the top-100 this year is much smaller: QR $5.7M (5.2%), TV Remotes $4.6M (3.9%), 2FA $12.4M (11.6%). In File Management, the leaf this cleaner targets, the new-entrant share is only 7.5%. 5) The UA claim holds as stated: Utilities' US ad-impression share is 9.8%, up 3.9pp, the largest rise of any app sub-category. But Utilities ranks only 22nd on US ad intensity, so impressions are not unusually high relative to revenue. iOS shares reproduce (File Management 88.8%, QR 86.8%, TV Remotes 92.3%), but these are IAP-only. The CPI/ARPPU falsification test is reasonable, though none of these numbers can confirm it.

The other cleaner apps grew +12% year on year, but their H2 revenue was 11.6% below H1, and Swipewipe, the swipe-UX comparable, is flat. verification.reasoning: The hypothesis proposes a photo cleaner, which sits in the File Management leaf. It borrows its accessibility evidence from QR, 2FA and TV-remote apps (new-entrant share 33.9%, 29.3% and 18.4%). File Management itself is the most concentrated leaf in the set: new-entrant share 7.5%, HHI 0.110, top-1 share 26.8% and top-3 share 49.2%. Its publisher mix is led by UAE (27.9%) and Ukraine (11.4%) app factories. Growth is captured mostly by one incumbent. Among cleaner-named apps in the top-100, revenue went from $292.8M to $384.5M, and Cleanup alone added +$63.2M of that +$91.7M (69%). Without Cleanup, cleaners grew only +13% ($219.4M to $247.9M), and Cleanup's downloads rose +217%, which signals a UA arms race. The mid-tier is already fading: Cleaner Guru (H2/H1 -12.6%), AI Cleaner (last3m -14.6%), Cleaner Kit (H2/H1 -24.8%), and the 2024 entrant Cleaner: Photo Cleanup (last3m -73%). The swipe-to-clean UX is not a new edge: Swipewipe already earns $16.8M, but its downloads are -15% and last3m is -6.5%. On the positive side, the tail is reachable. The rank-100 app earns about $0.52M a year (rank 50 about $1.2M), and 25 apps released in 2025 or later sit in the current top-100 with $27.2M (5.3%). The revenue test contradicts itself. Its pass thresholds (CPI $2.5, 10% trial, 25% trial-to-paid) imply about $100 CAC per payer. At $6.99 a week, 60-day ARPPU is at most about $60 gross, or $42-51 net of Apple's cut, even with zero churn. So a test that 'passes' still falsifies the claim. A 2-week window (the claim says 4 weeks) cannot observe 60-day ARPPU. It would yield about 40 payers on $4k, too few to estimate renewal. Ad-monetized demand matters little here because cleaners are subscription-IAP. Utilities downloads were -1.8% while revenue rose +34%, so the growth is monetization and pricing, not new demand. Platform risk is real: App Review acts on deceptive cleaner subscriptions, and a paywall 'after the first 100 swipes' is not a hard paywall.

hypotheses.claim: A European-themed merge-2 (localized village or bakery restoration story) beats a generic merge creative by >= 20% playable-ad IPM in DE/FR, at CPI below the US level.

evidence.metric: FR / NO / HU Match Merge 2 yoy
Local-publisher share of niche top-300 revenue

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium-low. Merge is the team's core strength, but the niche is concentrated (top-3 61%), entrants hold only 16% and LTV needs deep content. RPD $4.70 WW.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Merge-2 board with a European restoration narrative (German village, French patisserie), 30 levels plus 1 event loop, playable ads built from the first 60s.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad A/B (themed vs generic) in DE and FR, $2k each, 2 weeks: IPM, CPI, D1. Then a 3-week soft launch in NO+HU measuring D7 ROAS.
hypotheses.risks: Incumbent UA budgets (Gossip Harbor). Long content treadmill. Growth is 87% incumbent-driven, so a newcomer may only capture the long tail. Local cut of the WW themed merge-2 hypothesis; kept separate because the market (DE/FR/NO/HU, no local publishers) is the claim.

verification.reasoning: The country growth figures check out (country_niche_dynamics.csv, Match Merge 2): DE went from $76.7M to $169.9M (+121.6%, H2/H1 +25.0%), FR +110.9%, NO +114.5%, HU +166.0%, against WW +87.9% ($1,418.6M to $2,666.0M). But the growth comes from incumbents, not from a gap for new local players. In country_leaders.csv (current revenue, Match Merge 2), Gossip Harbor alone grew from $29.7M to $85.4M in DE, which is about 64% of the +$86.7M merge-2 gain within the top-300. In FR it grew from $19.7M to $52.2M, about 65% of +$47.8M. Every merge-2 title in the DE/FR top-300 comes from China, Israel, Finland, Hong Kong or Singapore, and was released between 2019 and 2024. "No local publishers" says nothing about whether a newcomer can get in. Merge Mansion (Finland) and Hollywood Merge (Ireland) show European publishers do compete, and in HU Hollywood Merge reached only $0.2M. Worldwide the niche is concentrated: top-1 41.8%, top-3 61.4%, HHI 0.208, and 86.6% of growth came from apps present in both periods. The successful entrants (Flambé $135.7M, Mystery Town $87.3M) are funded studios from China and Hong Kong. Ad intensity is also high and rising (ad_intensity_us 1.26, rank 36, impression share +1.38pp), so this looks like a UA arms race. The proposed test only partly measures revenue. A themed-vs-generic playable-ad A/B measures IPM and CPI, which are clicks and installs, not revenue. A 3-week soft launch in NO+HU with 30 levels and one event loop cannot give a meaningful D7 ROAS for a genre whose payback runs over 180+ days. NO+HU are also tiny markets: the whole niche earns $19.9M and $8.3M a year there. The "CPI below US" premise is shaky as a revenue argument: revenue per download is about $10.8 in DE vs $14.4 in the US, and $27.5 in NO, so cheaper CPI may simply mean lower LTV. Merge-2 is mostly IAP-monetized, so hidden ad revenue is not a big confounder here. The bigger blind spot is that IAP data cannot show UA spend.

hypotheses.title: Hole / Eat & Grow level puzzle with goal jars and a booster economy
hypotheses.market: Game sub-genre Eat & Grow (Physics/unravel and Screw as comparators)
hypotheses.claim: Hole games have moved from hypercasual into IAP level puzzles and demand is expanding, not just shifting: Eat & Grow $96M -> $179M (+87%, H2/H1 +29%), apps present in both periods +81% revenue on -8.8% downloads, US RPD $3.95 vs Screw $3.46 while Screw is past peak (H2/H1 -13%). A hole level-puzzle where objects must be eaten in colour/goal order to fill jars, with boosters, can find a viable CPI band and reach $0.5-1M/month within 6-10 months. Falsified if its playable IPM sits below a sort/screw control, or Eat & Grow H2/H1 turns negative.

$95.8M->$179.3M (+87.3%); apps in both periods rev +81.1% with dl -8.8%; All in Hole $98.0M at RPD $8.73

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium: cheap, playable-ad-friendly mechanic and moderate US ad intensity (rank 48), but concentrated (All in Hole 55% of top-100, HHI 0.319; France 59.6% of country mix) and entrant ramps are slow (Hole It 3D / Hole Stars $14.6M each, 10-11 months to $1M/month).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Hole puzzle where objects must be eaten in color order to fill goal jars (sort + hole hybrid), 30 levels.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad IPM/CPI test against an entrants-01 sort control ($2K each, US) over 10 days. If CPI is within 20% of the control, run a 2-week iOS soft launch in CA for D1/D7 and ARPDAU.
hypotheses.risks: One leader improving at the same time; decay risk (Hole People H2/H1 -77%); patient UA needed; moderate base. The unravel/physics arm of the monetization analyst's claim is covered by the physics and material-skin hypotheses. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers check out: Eat & Grow went from $95.8M to $179.3M (+87.3%), H2/H1 +29.3%, last3m +48.4%, US RPD $3.95 vs Screw $3.46. The "expanding, not shifting" story is weaker than it sounds, though. Three apps (All in Hole, Hole It 3D, Hole Stars) account for $67.3M of the $83.5M top-100 delta (81%). The "apps in both periods +81%" figure counts Hole It 3D and Hole Stars as incumbents, but they had only $29K and $2K of prior revenue, so they are really two new launches from Israeli publishers. Entrants into the top-100 added just $6.4M. Accessibility for a small team is unproven. Top-1 holds 54.7% and top-3 71.0% (HHI 0.319). Of 76 apps released since Oct-2024, only 2 reach the claimed $0.5M+/month run-rate (about $6M/yr), and both needed roughly 10-11 months of paid UA. Meanwhile Hole People shows the decay risk (H2/H1 -77%). Momentum is softening at the margin. Niche revenue peaked in Jul-26 at $18.12M and fell to $16.57M in Sep (-8.6%). Downloads are falling (yoy -7.1%, H2/H1 -10.8%, last3m -16.4%). The niche also leans on the most expensive UA market: the US is $117.2M of $179.3M (65%). The proposed test does not measure revenue. A $2K playable IPM/CPI test against a sort control measures installs and clicks. A 2-week CA soft launch of a 30-level build can show D1/D7, but its ARPDAU says little about a booster economy whose IAP usually starts past early levels. So the revenue arm only starts after 4 weeks, and the $0.5-1M/month claim is not testable inside the window. The falsifier is also lopsided. Sort is a $754M niche growing +283% with US ad-intensity rank 10, so a hole ad losing to it on IPM proves little. And niche H2/H1 is unlikely to turn negative soon. Regulatory risk is low: no gambling, sweepstakes or AI-content issues. The measurement boundary cuts both ways. Hole.io has 108.2M downloads but only $2.8M of IAP, so a large ad-monetized hole audience is invisible in revenue. That supports demand for the mechanic, but it also means IAP growth may come from hybridcasual conversion of an existing audience, not new demand.

hypotheses.title: Unlicensed classic + one rule twist (association/sort Solitaire)
hypotheses.market: Game sub-genre Solitaire (and other classic card/tile niches)
hypotheses.claim: Most Solitaire growth is one licensed hit (Disney Solitaire +$164M, 132% of the delta) while pre-2024-07 apps fell $260M -> $172M, but an unlicensed hybrid with one new rule layer (Solitaire Associations Journey: $43.8M, 82.6M downloads, 1 month to $1M/month) broke in without IP. A TriPeaks/classic build with an association or sort goal layer and a light meta will beat a plain classic control by >= 20% on D7 and ARPDAU and pass a US/GB 35+ playable-ad test.

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium-low: buildable by a small team, but winner-take-most (top1 51%, top-3 82%, HHI 0.321; only 2 new apps >= $5M); legacy incumbents are falling (Grand Harvest -43%, Fishdom Solitaire -52%). Word-dependent twists need localisation.

hypotheses.revenue_test: Two-week US/CA iOS soft launch of the twist build alongside a plain classic control at a $3K UA split. Measure D1/D7 and ARPDAU; pass if the twist beats the control by 20% or more on D7 and ARPDAU.
hypotheses.risks: License-driven growth is not replicable; expensive 35+ UA; twist ideas are easy to copy; only two non-IP winners so far. Heavy ad monetization in solitaire is invisible here. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: The niche numbers hold up: Solitaire grew from $330.0M to $454.7M (+37.8%, H2/H1 +17.8%). But almost none of that growth is open to a newcomer. Disney Solitaire grew from $68.3M to $232.6M and alone takes 51.3% of the top 100. Strip it out and the rest of the niche shrank from $260.6M to $220.5M (-15%). Strip out Associations Journey too and everyone else fell about 32%. Downloads are also shrinking: H2/H1 -29%, last 3 months -15% year on year. So the growth is IP-driven revenue per download, not a wave of new players. The one hit without a licence, Solitaire Associations Journey ($43.8M), earned only about $0.53 per download from 82.6M downloads (#122 worldwide by downloads). Reaching that download volume takes a very large user-acquisition budget, which a small studio does not have. It does not show that a rule twist on its own breaks through. Sort and word twists already exist, and they stall around $1M or less: Color Sort Solitaire $0.6M, Word Solitaire Now! $0.6M on 3.1M downloads, Solitaire Town Tycoon $1.0M. The deciding problem is the test. $3K split over two arms for two weeks buys only a few hundred US iOS installs per arm (CPI is my assumption, not in the data). The US niche earns only about $1.98 per download per year, so each arm would book tens of dollars of in-app revenue. That is far too little to detect a 20% ARPDAU difference, and solitaire ARPDAU is largely ad revenue that this data cannot see. The test would measure D1/D7 retention and clicks, not revenue. The niche itself is real and growing (US +13.8%, GB +93.8%), so a redesigned test (a larger budget, ad revenue counted, a gate on payer conversion) could reopen the idea. As written, the revenue hypothesis cannot be tested.

Every headline number reproduces from the CSVs. Solitaire is $454.7M vs $330.0M (+37.8%), H2/H1 +17.8%, top1 share 0.513, top-3 0.817, HHI 0.322. Disney's monthly revenue peaked in Mar-2026 at $26.2M and was $16.0M by Sep-2026 (-39%). The niche peaked in May-2026 at $44.9M and fell four months in a row to $35.9M (-20%). Jul-Sep 2026 was 10.7% below Apr-Jun, so the "accelerating" H2/H1 label hides a turn downward. Niche downloads have H2/H1 -29%.
2. **The "unlicensed twist" rests on one app, and the clones failed.** Solitaire Associations Journey reproduces exactly ($43.78M, 82.6M downloads; $26K in Oct-2025 then $1.85M in Nov-2025; Sep-2026 at 0.97 of peak). It is a word-association format, and its look-alikes tagged Word all earn $1.6M or less: Connect Word Association $1.56M, Associations-Colorwood $1.37M, Words Klondike: Associations $0.54M, Solitaire Word Associations $0.24M. The closest data point to the proposed sort twist is Color Sort Solitaire at $0.6M.
3. **The proposed test has no data behind it.** Nothing in this data room can support the D7/ARPDAU +20% prediction.

US Solitaire grew only +13.8% ($226.6M). Japan (+178%) and Korea (+276%, on a $2.5M prior base) are likely mostly Disney-IP-driven. The source-ids' data/raw link was also checked: monthly figures there are in cents and are consistent with the CSV totals.

verification.reasoning: Every quoted number reproduces within 1%. Solitaire went $330.04M to $454.67M (+37.8%) with RPD 0.995 to 1.276. Disney Solitaire went $68.25M to $232.58M on 31.29M downloads, so RPD is $7.43. In Match Pair the top-10 earners have an RPD of 4.248 against 0.397 for the top-20 download leaders, and 81.2% of downloads in the downloads top-100 sit in apps with RPD below $0.10. The three-niche total is $1,073.4M, up 10.45%. The mechanism behind those numbers does not hold up, though. Solitaire's growth is a single licensed-IP launch: Disney Solitaire alone added +$164.3M while the whole niche added +$124.6M. Without it the niche fell by about $39.7M. If you also drop Solitaire Associations Journey (a word/associations hybrid that is new under the tag and brought +$43.8M), the rest of the niche falls from $261.8M to $178.3M (-32%). The solitaire titles that already ran a meta layer are shrinking: Solitaire Grand Harvest -43% ($165.4M to $94.0M), Fishdom Solitaire -52%, Solitaire Home Design -53%, Solitaire Cruise -38%, Tiki Solitaire -25%. So "meta layer causes IAP" is contradicted unless IP and heavy UA come with it. In Match Pair the high-RPD earners (Match Factory! 12.8, Triple Match City 11.3, Triple Match 3D 23.2) are 3D match-and-sort games, a different mechanic from the classic mahjong/tile apps they are compared with (Vita Mahjong 0.012, Mahjong Blast 0.0001). Sensor Tower counts only in-store IAP, so an ad-only classic shows near-zero RPD by construction. Vita Mahjong's 149.5M downloads at $1.8M say nothing about its ad revenue, so the ">5x RPD" claim cannot be checked in this data. Jigsaw's +40.8% growth comes from one new entrant, Jigsaw Block Sort (added 2025-12, $6.6M), which looks like a block-sort puzzle and may be a taxonomy artifact. Entrants contributed +$7.19M while the incumbents changed by -$1.82M on a $13.2M base, and niche RPD is only $0.064. Match Pair as a whole is declining: -4.5% year on year, -14.9% H2 vs H1, -20.4% for last3m (Jul–Sep 2026 vs Jul–Sep 2025).

In niche_monthly_game_sub_genre.csv the niche earned only $0.43M, $0.41M, $0.65M and $2.69M in Oct 2024 to Jan 2025, because Color Block Jam's first revenue month was 2024-12 (app_series_features). The prior window is a launch ramp. Like-for-like Apr-Sep 2026 vs Apr-Sep 2025 is $121.3M vs $108.6M, only +11.7%, and last3m is +19.4%.

(2) Single-hit concentration. Block Out!'s s_rev_h2_h1=19.57 implies about $2.3M in H1 and $46.5M in H2. Without it, the niche goes from about $90.0M to $74.7M, an H2/H1 of roughly -17%. Its YoY ex-Block Out! is +21.7%, and its last3m is roughly -27% (my estimate). So the acceleration is one app, not 'each new variant'. The other 34 top-100 entrants together earned only about $7.3M (entrants_rev_cur $56.1M minus $48.8M). Earlier variants fade fast: Drop Away H2/H1 -55%, Water Out -65%, Wood Away -79% YoY, Sky Rush -94%.

The 'leader fades' part holds: Color Block Jam is -6% YoY, H2/H1 -16% and last3m -46%. That decline is partly flattered by its prior having only 11 observed months.

Measurement notes. Block Out!'s revenue is 99.99% iOS (android_rev_share 0.00006), so Android is either not launched or tracked under another ID. The Block tag mixes IAP jam/escape games with ad-monetized block-blast games. Block Blast! has 339.5M downloads but $74.6K IAP. That makes the niche's IAP revenue a jam/escape signal only, and downloads are flat (+7%, H2/H1 -13%). Turkey holds 80.8% of the top-5 revenue, and the rotation may be within the same publisher cluster; the CSVs carry no publisher names, so this is unverified. The claim that a novel exit rule beats Block Out!-style creatives in playable-ad tests cannot be tested from this data.

Fit for a small casual/playable team is still plausible: it is a mechanic-led niche with rotating hits. But the evidence supports 'one hit every about 12 months with roughly a 6-month half-life', not 'the niche rewards each variant'.

hypotheses.title: Collector scanner + gamified binder (TCG / sports cards / coins)
hypotheses.market: Collectible-scanner cluster across Lifestyle & Services, Object ID, Hobbies leaves
hypotheses.claim: Collector scanning and pricing is fast-growing and fragmented. A scanner plus set-completion binder can reach at least 8% trial at CPI of $3 or less on US iOS. Falsified otherwise.
hypotheses.accessibility: High: fragmented, entrants reach $2-3M within a year; small absolute market. Strong fit for collection mechanics.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Scan a card, get ID and price history, file it in a virtual binder with set completion, rarity reveals and a weekly 'value up' digest; $4.99/week or $39.99/year.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 3-week build; US iOS with $2k ASA on card-value keywords plus TikTok pack-opening creatives. Pass: CPI ≤ $3, trial ≥ 8%, D7 ≥ 25%.
hypotheses.risks: Price-data licensing, recognition accuracy, TCG fad cycle, card-image IP, small total market. Name-regex cluster across several leaves; reclassification risk.

verification.reasoning:
The growth is real. I rebuilt the cluster from niche_top_apps.csv (field=app_iq_category, order=revenue) with a name regex and dropped false positives such as WEBTOON, crypto miners and PDF scanners. That gives 70 apps at $79.5M vs $38.8M (+105%), close to the claimed $86.7M/+102%. Inside it, TCG and sports cards (43 apps) went from $11.4M to $43.7M (+285%), while coins went only from $25.6M to $31.7M (+24%), and the two coin leaders are already declining (CoinSnap s_rev_h2_h1 = -34%, CoinIn -12.5% with last3m -30%). So the opportunity is a card-only wedge, not 'TCG / sports cards / coins'.

Entry is open to newcomers. Apps released since 2024-10 earn $19.3M (24% of the cluster), and HoloDex ($3.5M), Cardly ($2.2M), FoilSnap ($2.0M) and StarSnap ($1.9M) all reached $2-3.5M within about 12 months. But 53 of the 70 apps make under $1M. Most of the new revenue goes to AI-identifier app factories in China, Hong Kong, Turkey and the UAE (China plus Hong Kong hold 28% of cluster revenue) that are good at paid user acquisition. The fastest grower is Card Ladder (+$7.7M, H2/H1 +141%), and its edge is proprietary sales-price data, not the scanner.

Card Ladder and Collectr together account for about 30% of the +$40.6M growth, so the price-history feature at the core of the prototype is exactly the part a small team cannot license cheaply or build in 3 weeks. The test as written measures CPI, install-to-trial and D7, not paid conversion or revenue. $2k at a $3 CPI buys about 670 installs and about 53 trials, too few to read trial-to-paid or the renewal rate of a $4.99/week subscription. It needs a trial-to-paid gate on day 10 or later, and probably a larger budget.

Hidden ad-monetized demand matters little here, because these are hard-paywall subscription apps that store IAP data captures well. The real platform risks are Apple's 4.3 rule against spam in the crowded scanner category, card-image and trademark rights (Pokémon, Topps/Panini) and the terms of service of scraped price data. There is also a fad risk: Pokémon TCG Pocket revenue fell 61% year on year in leaders.csv, which shows TCG demand can cycle. For a casual or merge studio, the binder and collection mechanics are a reasonable fit. The edge would be retention, not acquisition, and it is unproven.

verification.reasoning: The market numbers hold up: the Nutrition & Diet top-100 grew from $549.3M to $610.1M (+11.1%), HHI is 0.114, the top app holds 28.5% and the top 3 hold 47.9% (niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv). The country numbers also check out: Personal Health & Fitness went DE $158.0M→$193.9M (+22.7%), FR $88.9M→$115.3M (+29.7%) and US $1,477.7M→$1,481.0M (+0.2%). But most of the growth went to challengers that were already established, not to new names. Yazio (+$25.8M), MacroFactor (+$11.8M), Cal AI (+$9.8M) and Foodvisor (+$10.0M) together add about $57M of the net +$60.8M, and apps present in both periods account for 66.9% of the absolute delta. In FR, Foodvisor and Yazio together add about $5.9M of the $26.4M FR delta (country_leaders.csv). It soft-launches in CA/UK, not the DE/FR markets the thesis is about, and those markets grew only +6.0% (CA) and +7.5% (GB) in the parent category. It also passes or fails on CPI, trial start and D7, never on trial-to-paid conversion or first-year revenue. With $3k at $3 CPI you get about 1,000 installs and about 80 trials, too few to estimate paid conversion. Store data also misses web2app subscriptions, which are common for AI trackers, so challenger revenue may be undercounted (in-store revenue is not where the competition is decided). Other risks: health-data rules (GDPR special-category data in DE/FR), regulation of nutrition and health claims, and eating-disorder exposure for minors. None of these block the idea, but they make it costlier. Accessibility is plausible but not proven, and the test as written would measure clicks rather than revenue, so the verdict is 'weakened', not 'supported'.

In country_leaders.csv (top-300), Nutrition & Diet adds only +$8.6M of DE's +$35.9M parent delta and +$4.8M of FR's +$26.4M; Gyms & Fitness adds about as much or more (DE +$9.9M, FR +$7.8M). Inside nutrition each market is effectively one home incumbent: Yazio is $44.2M of $49.3M in DE (+$13.3M, more than the net +$8.6M), and Foodvisor plus Yazio make up 92% of FR. The 'Europe grows' signal is therefore largely two local incumbents' home-market growth, not open demand that a newcomer can capture. Calo's +650% sits on a $1.08M prior base, Welmi's +2125% on $0.17M, and BitePal and Numify have no prior top-100 base. App-level H2/H1 is confounded by the January resolution spike in H1 (parent monthly: Jan-2026 $306.4M vs about $250M in a typical month), so 'Cal AI H2/H1 -7%' is partly seasonal (its last3m YoY is +6.8%). The regex 'calorie cluster' is not reproducible as stated: my regex gives $461.3M to $538.9M (+16.8%), not +21%. The revenue test (soft launch in CA/UK) contradicts the DE/FR-first claim, and those markets grew only +6.0% and +7.5% at parent level. The trial/CPI/D7 thresholds cannot be derived from this data.

hypotheses.title: Learn-to-draw / craft as a gamified micro-lesson feed
hypotheses.market: Digital Art & Drawing leaf + learn-to-draw cluster
hypotheses.claim: Guided skill-learning hobby apps are growing on challengers. A playable-ad-led drawing app can reach CPI of $2.5 or less and at least 6% trial. Falsified otherwise.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium: challenger-led (entrants share of abs delta 0.08), HHI 0.11; AR-tracing entrant hit 34.9M downloads. Strong playable-ad fit.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Daily 5-minute tracing lessons as a vertical feed with scores and a weekly masterpiece challenge; weekly/yearly subscription.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 3 playable ads (trace a cat) to a build, US/UK, $3k, 2 weeks. Pass: CTR ≥ 1.5%, CPI ≤ $2.5, trial ≥ 6%.
hypotheses.risks: Simply out-spending on UA; low leaf RPD ($0.64); cost of lesson content.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce. In niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv, Digital Art & Drawing has top-100 revenue of $157.0M vs $112.8M (+39.1%) and HHI 0.114. Growth decomposition is $41.4M from apps present in both periods against $3.7M from entrants (entrant share 0.083), so this is the same apps growing, not a re-tagging artifact. Rebuilding the learn/trace cluster with a name regex over niche_top_apps.csv gives $77.0M vs $33.5M (+130%), within 10% of the claimed $80.8M vs $37.0M. A strict "learn/lesson/how to draw" regex gives $55.7M vs $21.7M (+157%), so the exact figure depends on which apps the regex catches. The real problem is concentration. Simply Draw alone adds +$26.7M of the niche's +$44.2M top-100 delta (60.5%), and with ArtWorkout (+$6.8M) the two apps make up 76%. So "growing on challengers" is mostly one hit plus one follower, not a broad trend. Momentum is also mixed. Simply Draw's H2/H1 is only +5.4% (last3m yoy +87%), so most of its jump is already in the base. ArtWorkout is slowing (s_rev_h2_h1 -18.7%, peak month 2026-01), while Procreate (-15%) and Illustrator (-27%) shrink. The YarnPal "$0.3M to $7.1M" figure is a launch-year base effect: it was released 2024-12, its first revenue month is 2025-04, H2/H1 is -4.9%, and it sits in Hobbies & Interests Services, not this leaf. The "AR-tracing hit with 34.9M downloads" (Draw Anime) earned $5.3K IAP and is not a revenue entrant (prior downloads 21.5M, released 2024-09). It shows downloads can be bought or ad-monetized, not that IAP revenue is accessible. The CPI ≤ $2.5 and trial ≥ 6% thresholds are test design and have no support in this data room.

AR-tracing download hits earn almost no IAP. verification.reasoning:
The niche's growth is real, but almost all of it went to one incumbent. Digital Art & Drawing top-100 revenue rose from $112.8M to $157.0M, a $44.2M gain. Simply Draw (Israel, released 2022) accounts for $26.7M of that gain, or 60.5%. Apps present in both periods account for 93.8% of the absolute change. The 16 apps that entered the top 100 earned only $3.66M combined (8.3%).

The concentration figure also hides how small the market is below the leaders. HHI of 0.11 sounds open, but top3_share is 0.52 and top10_share is 0.78. The #20 app earns about $0.91M a year, the #50 about $0.26M and the #100 about $0.055M. A realistic outcome for a new entrant is therefore under $1M a year in gross in-store revenue, not a share of $157M.

The "AR-tracing entrant hit 34.9M downloads" evidence cuts against the revenue thesis. Draw Anime earned $0.005M in in-app purchases (IAP), and Artrace earned $0.94M on 37.8M downloads. The 41 AR/trace apps in the downloads top 100 have 169.9M downloads but only $14.8M of IAP, about $0.09 per download. That demand is ad-monetized or free, which this data does not show. Playable ads tuned for a cheap "trace a cat" hook are likely to pull in that low-intent audience. Payers cluster on iOS subscription apps: Simply Draw makes about $1.57 per download with 90% of revenue on iOS, and ArtWorkout about $0.59.

Momentum among the challengers is mixed. Simply Draw's H2/H1 is +5% and its last-3-month YoY is +87%, but ArtWorkout's H2/H1 is -18.7%. YarnPal ($7.1M) sits in Hobbies & Interests Services, not this leaf, and its H2/H1 is -4.9%.

The proposed revenue test measures clicks and trial starts, not revenue. $3k at a $2.5 CPI buys about 1,200 installs, and 6% of that is about 72 trials. The test has no trial-to-paid or first-renewal criterion and is too small to read one. Building a 5-minute lesson feed with content in 4 weeks is feasible.

Risks: drawing and tracing apps attract children (COPPA, kids-category rules), AI-generated lesson content invites platform scrutiny, and a well-funded leader is buying US/UK iOS traffic at the same time.

hypotheses.title: One-phone impostor/party word game with pack unlocks or a pack pass
hypotheses.market: Game sub-genre Social Party (Western imposter/charades wave; US/GB)
hypotheses.claim: Western one-phone party games grow on small bases (Social Party $197M -> $245M, downloads +41%, US time spent +51%; GB +102%, DE +69%), led by 2025 imposter releases (Imposter Game Fakeit $8.6M at RPD $0.46). A pass-and-play impostor word game with a free starter deck and paid packs (one-off unlocks or a weekly pass) earns >= $0.30 per iOS download. Falsified if pack/pass conversion stays < 1% after 2 weeks or fake-door intent misses the pre-set threshold.

evidence.metric: Social Party revenue; downloads; US time spent

evidence.value: Imposter Game Fakeit $8.6M (2025-08, Poland, +10,440%); Splash $4.9M (+177%); Imposter Who? $2.8M; Charades Guess +146%

hypotheses.accessibility: High build feasibility (about 2 weeks, no heavy art) and low UA pressure (ad_intensity_us 0.39, rank 71; iOS 75.9% of revenue). Asian leaders (WePlay 39%, HHI 0.172) are a separate market; the Western tail is fragmented.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Pass-the-phone impostor word game with 10 free packs, a weekly subscription for 100+ packs and TikTok-ready party clips.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 2-3 week US/GB iOS + Android launch with ASO plus $1-2k of TikTok creatives; measure pack conversion and RPD.
hypotheses.risks: Viral and seasonal fad (H2/H1 only +6.5%); clone flood (tag count 2,562 -> 4,941); low RPD and LTV; most dollars sit in Asian voice-chat apps. Pack vs subscription pricing is unresolved between analysts.

verification.reasoning:
There is a real door for small teams. In the current 12 months, 21 new entrants made $26.7M, or 11.1% of the Social Party top-100. They come from small Western publishers: Fakeit (Poland), Splash (Germany) and Imposter Who? (US). The build is cheap and the niche is not UA-heavy: ad_intensity_us is 0.39, rank 71.

Two things in the headline are overstated. First, most of the growth is not Western imposter games. Of the +$47.8M year-on-year gain, Goose Goose Duck (鹅鸭杀, China, released 2021, 99% iOS) added +$24.2M, or 51%. China was the largest-growing country, $24.6M to $46.7M. All Western imposter entrants together added only about $18.0M. Second, the Western wave looks like a fad that has passed its peak. Niche revenue peaked at $23.6M in April 2026 and fell to $19.0M in September. Imposter Who?, Spy Undercover and Party Edition all peaked in December 2025 or January 2026, and their H2/H1 revenue changed by -17%, -48% and -21%. Only Fakeit (+9%) and Splash (+15%) are still growing.

The $0.30 RPD bar is an outlier, not the norm. Measured as worldwide revenue per worldwide download (not per iOS download as the hypothesis states), only Fakeit clears it at $0.46. Splash makes $0.28, Imposter Who? $0.16, Party Edition $0.10 and Spy Undercover $0.04 on 31.6M downloads. Spy Undercover suggests much of the demand earns from ads, which IAP data cannot see. Android ad-impression share also rose about 4.6x (0.029% to 0.131%), so UA competition is growing.

The test does measure real revenue, because pack and pass purchases are real IAP. But $1-2k of TikTok spend buys roughly 1,000-2,000 installs. That is only about 10-20 buyers at the 1% bar, and the fake-door branch measures intent clicks, not revenue. Platform risks are App Store guideline 4.3 (spam/copycat) rejection in a niche where the tag count grew from 2,562 to 4,941 apps, a teen audience, and churn on a weekly pass for a game played only now and then.

Measurement boundary: these figures are App Store and Google Play IAP only. Ad revenue from the high-download, low-RPD clones does not appear, and China revenue is iOS-only, which inflates GGD's share of the iOS-heavy mix.
