hypotheses.title: Physics puzzle hybrids (rope/tangle/smash, castle artillery) are a small but accelerating door
hypotheses.market: Game sub-genres: Physics (+ Artillery Shooter)
hypotheses.claim: Physics-based puzzle hybrids are accelerating, and a new entrant can get 10M+ downloads within 4 months. Falsified if Physics H2/H1 turns negative by Q1-2027 or the playable test IPM is below Sort benchmarks.

evidence.value: Royal Smash! 17.1M dl (released 2026-06), Smash Fest! 22.8M dl/$5.8M, Wool Escape 3D $8.0M

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium. Physics prototypes are cheap, but Angry Birds holds 50% of the niche as top-1, the base is small, and US ad rank is 19.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: A rope/tangle or smash physics puzzle with satisfying destruction, delivered as a playable ad first.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad IPM/CPI test in US + Tier-2 ($2K) over 10 days. If IPM is in the top quartile, run a 2-week Android/iOS soft launch measuring D7 and blended ad + IAP ARPDAU.
hypotheses.risks: Small base. Single-app-driven growth in Artillery. Physics feel is costly to tune. Overlaps the material-skin (yarn/unravel) hypothesis through Wool Escape 3D. Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: Every headline number reproduces exactly. Physics revenue went from $69.7M to $107.2M (+53.8%), with H2/H1 +27.0% and last3m +84.0%. Downloads were flat YoY (-0.5%). Turkey's share of the Physics top 100 went from 0.0% to 14.2%, and Castle Clashers! made $34.5M of Artillery's $52.7M (65.4%). So this is not an arithmetic or reclassification artifact. The growing titles carry the Physics tag in both periods, and top-100 coverage is 99.3%. The growth pattern is less clean than the hypothesis suggests. hypotheses.title: KR, TW, JP Tower Defense: the most fragmented growing niche, open to merge-defense
hypotheses.market: South Korea and Taiwan (secondary: Japan)
hypotheses.claim: A co-op or random merge-defense prototype gets playable-ad CTR within 20% of Lucky Defense-style creatives and D1 >= 40% in a 3-week KR/TW soft launch.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium. Lowest concentration among growing niches and entrants take 41% of the top-100; a light merge-defense loop is within reach of a small team, but KR incumbents are local and live-ops heavy.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Merge-defense: merge random units on a grid to defend lanes, 2-player co-op via async ghosts, gacha-lite unit collection.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad CTR/CPI test in KR and TW ($2k each, 2 weeks), then a 3-week TW soft launch measuring D1/D7 and payer conversion.
hypotheses.risks: KR players favor local brands. Mid-core monetization needs live ops. JP is held by Chinese and Singaporean publishers with big IP. Local cut of the WW merge-defense hypothesis.

verification.reasoning:
The headline revenue numbers check out: KR TD is $84.6M to $122.5M (+44.9%) and TW is $41.3M to $58.8M (+42.6%), both accelerating. JP is +36.4% but its momentum is steady (H2/H1 +0.6%). Three things undercut the case for a new entrant.

1. **"Most fragmented growing niche" is false.** Among growing game sub-genres with at least $100M, Action RPG has a lower HHI (0.052, vs TD 0.064). The low worldwide TD concentration comes from mixing Arknights, survivor hybrids (Cell Survivor, BangBang Survivor) and Chinese, HK and SG publishers. That mix is China 48.1%, HK 16.8%, KR 14.0% by publisher country.

2. **KR TD is close to a duopoly, and the duo already makes the proposed game.** In the KR top 300, Lucky Defense ($49.1M) and 협타디 ($16.9M) together make $66.0M, about 54% of all KR TD revenue and about 75% of the TD revenue that appears in the top 300. Both are Korean random/co-op merge-defense titles, so the "co-op random merge-defense" slot is taken. The KR entrants that do show up have big publishers behind them: 귀판오분전 (China, $4.9M), Cell Survivor (Singapore, $5.3M) and Galaxy Defense (HK, $3.7M).

3. **Growth comes from spend per player, not new players.** KR TD downloads fell 9.7% and TW fell 4.9%. Lucky Defense's worldwide downloads dropped 66% (3.80M to 1.29M) while its revenue rose 12%. That points to deeper spending by existing players, which is hard for a newcomer without live-ops to capture.

**The test does not measure revenue.** The claim is scored on playable-ad CTR within 20% of Lucky Defense creatives and D1 of at least 40%. Both are click and retention signals. Payer conversion in a 3-week TW soft launch of a gacha-lite build is too short and too small to read mid-core lifetime value. Building a playable, a gacha collection and async co-op, plus 2 weeks of CPI testing and 3 weeks of soft launch, also runs past 4 weeks.

**Other risks:**
- Gacha needs published draw probabilities in KR (law in force since March 2024) and similar disclosure in TW.
- TD's US ad intensity rank is 31 (1.56). That is moderate, so some ad-funded demand probably exists, but it doesn't change the IAP-driven local picture.

verification.reasoning:
Every quoted number reproduces exactly. JP Sort is $6.18M -> $18.94M (+206%, H2/H1 +63%) with 27.4M -> 48.1M downloads, 8.0% of JP game downloads (country_niche_dynamics.csv). WW Sort is $753.9M, +283%, last3m +272%, top-1 Pixel Flow! 25.0%, HHI 0.093 and 76.3% new-entrant share (niche_dynamics_game_sub_genre.csv; niche_leaders_full_game_sub_genre.csv). Recomputing the penetration indices against an ex-JP/ex-CN games baseline gives JP rev PI 0.148 and dl PI 2.15, and KR 0.16 and 1.66.

The 'monetized at 0.15x' headline is mostly a denominator artifact. It divides Sort's share of JP game revenue, a market inflated by gacha, where a game download earns $11.66 against about $0.90 in the baseline (roughly 13x). Per download, JP Sort earns $0.39 (prior $0.23), about 0.90x the ex-JP/CN Sort baseline of $0.44. That is the same as KR ($0.39), above TW ($0.27) and FR ($0.34), and only low next to the Anglo tier-1 markets: US $2.06, AU $1.91, GB $1.47. So the data show no JP-specific supply gap. They show that Sort IAP monetizes well only in English-speaking markets, and that JP looks like the rest of East Asia and continental Europe.

JP also grew slower than every Western market (+206% vs US +269%, GB +324%, DE +359%). The 'no leader' point is trivially true: the whole JP niche ($18.9M) is only about 3.5x the top-300 revenue cutoff ($5.4M). The six Sort apps that appear in JP's top-300 downloads account for only about 11.7M of the 48.1M downloads, so the market is a foreign long tail, not a vacant throne.

The test in the claim (CPI <= 1.3x US, D1 >= 35%) cannot be checked against this data at all. Its fallback ('otherwise the gap is cultural') is a non-sequitur, because the data already suggest that most of the gap is a market-structure denominator effect. The IAP-only boundary cuts both ways: JP ad revenue is invisible, but so is ad revenue in the baseline.

verification.reasoning: The growth is real. In country_niche_dynamics.csv, JP Sort grew from $6.18M to $18.94M (+206%, H2/H1 +63%) and downloads grew from 27.4M to 48.1M, which is 8.0% of JP game downloads. But "monetized at 0.15x" is mostly a denominator artifact: Sort's share of JP game IAP (0.27%) is small because JP IAP is dominated by gacha. Measured per download, JP Sort earns $0.394, against $2.06 in the US, $0.87 in DE and $0.34 in FR. That is 1.9x the ex-US average of the 28 countries ($0.207), so outside the US there is no unique JP monetization hole. That suggests the Sort gap reflects JP downloads skewing to ad-monetized arrow and escape titles: Arrows Puzzle Escape has 2.84M JP downloads but only $23k of IAP. The IAP prize is small: no Sort app reaches the JP revenue top-300 (cutoff $5.4M), and the whole niche is $18.9M, so a 10% share is about $1.9M of IAP per year. The follow-up 2-week soft launch at $3-5k buys about 1-2k JP installs, enough to measure ad ARPDAU but too few to measure IAP conversion. It also needs a localized store build, so it is feasible in 4 weeks only as a cheap reskin. Regulatory and platform risk is low (no gambling mechanics), though JP's 2023 stealth-marketing rules apply to UA creatives.

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium. Cheap UA and no local incumbents, but leaders are the same global merge and match titles, and RPD is low ($0.31 games in MX).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Merge-2 with a Latin-American story (mercado or family restaurant), Spanish voice and copy, low-price IAP tiers.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 3-week soft launch in MX+CO ($3k): CPI, D7 ROAS, payer conversion; compare with a GB control cell ($2k).

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers check out. MX games are $549.7M (+9.7%) with downloads -14.5%, and MX Match Merge 2 went from $11.63M to $28.27M (+143%, H2/H1 +40%). The growth is not open to a newcomer, though: one global incumbent took most of it. Gossip Harbor (China) went from $5.52M to $17.35M in MX, which is 71% of the niche's +$16.6M and 61% of current MX Match Merge 2 revenue. The MX top five are all Chinese or Israeli global titles, and the global niche has top10_share=0.89 with Chinese publishers holding 67.3% of the top five. A local publisher share near 0% (MX 0.8%, CO 0.9% of top-300 revenue) means global UA spenders take everything. It is not a gap waiting for a local entrant. The ROAS claim also conflicts with the store data. Match Merge 2 revenue per download is $1.62 in MX and $0.61 in CO, against $9.84 in GB. That is 16% and 6% of GB, so reaching 60% of GB D7 ROAS would need a CPI near 27% of GB in MX and about 10% in CO, not just "less than half". CO is also too small to matter: the whole Match Merge 2 niche there is $3.6M a year. The test does measure IAP revenue, but it is badly underpowered. $3k at LatAm CPIs buys a few thousand installs and $2k in GB a few hundred, so at roughly 1-2% payer conversion D7 ROAS rests on a handful of GB payers. Merge-2 also pays back over months, not at D7, and building a merge-2 with a working IAP economy in about 4 weeks is a stretch even for a merge-skilled team. LatAm monetization leans more on ads than GB, and IAP-only data plus an IAP-only ROAS test miss that ad revenue. Argentina's +40% country revenue is largely FX and inflation, so the AR evidence is not growth a launch could capture.

hypotheses.title: Hybrid solitaire in GB, DE, FR: growth taken by 2024-25 entrants
hypotheses.market: United Kingdom (secondary: Germany, France)
hypotheses.claim: A solitaire-plus-merge or word hybrid reaches CPI <= $2.50 and D7 >= 15% in a GB soft launch. Failure means IP and incumbent UA lock the niche.

evidence.value: Solitaire Associations Journey (2025-08) $43.8M WW, 17.8M US downloads; Disney Solitaire $232.6M

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium. Cheap to build, but concentrated; the winners are hybrids or IP.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: TriPeaks solitaire whose cleared cards feed a merge-2 restoration board (the team's merge skill), or a word-association solitaire variant.
hypotheses.revenue_test: GB soft launch, 4 weeks, $5k UA: CPI, D7, ARPDAU. Run a playable-ad CTR test against Disney Solitaire-style creatives first.
hypotheses.risks: Disney IP. Incumbent UA spend. JP and KR growth is 83-93% one app, so it does not transfer. Local cut of the solitaire-twist hypothesis.

verification.reasoning: Every headline number reproduces exactly. GB Solitaire is $17.47M to $33.87M (+93.8%, H2/H1 +38.3%), FR is $6.57M to $13.17M (+100.5%), DE is $21.55M to $30.18M (+40.1%) (country_niche_dynamics.csv). WW is $330.0M to $454.7M (+37.8%), with new_entrants_share_of_top100=0.619, top3_share=0.817 and hhi_top100=0.322 (niche_leaders_full_game_sub_genre.csv). The mechanism is the problem, because the "entrants" growth in these countries is one licensed-IP hit. In country_leaders.csv, Disney Solitaire (released 2024-11) went from $3.70M to $20.86M in GB, a gain of +$17.17M. That is 105% of the niche's net +$16.40M, and Disney now holds 61.6% of GB solitaire revenue. In FR it added +$6.92M against net +$6.60M (105%, 68% share). In DE it added +$11.84M against net +$8.63M (137%), while Solitaire Grand Harvest fell $14.69M to $10.24M. Without Disney the niche shrinks: GB $13.78M to $13.01M (-5.6%), FR $4.50M to $4.18M (-7%), DE $18.44M to $15.23M (-17%), and WW $261.8M to $222.1M (-15.2%; Disney's WW delta of +$164.3M is 132% of the niche's +$124.6M, leaders.csv). That is the same one-app pattern the hypothesis names as a risk for JP/KR, so the European rows are not a broad niche trend either. The +94% GB growth is also partly a base effect: Disney's prior window holds only about 10 ramp-up months (first revenue 2024-12, peak 2026-03, H2/H1 +24%). The word-hybrid proof point, Solitaire Associations Journey, is US-centric: $31.52M of its $43.78M WW revenue is in the US, only $2.13M in GB, $1.45M in DE and $0.72M in FR. Its 17.8M US downloads are correct, but they say little about a GB soft launch. The CPI ≤ $2.50 / D7 ≥ 15% thresholds cannot be checked in this data room, and all figures are App Store and Google Play in-app purchases only, so ad revenue from ad-monetized solitaire is invisible. Taxonomy is not the issue: the top apps really did grow, and this is not a reclassification artifact. But the mechanism is "one Disney-IP meta hybrid plus a declining incumbent base", not open space being taken by entrants.

hypotheses.title: Gamified self-care pet / habit companion
hypotheses.market: Meditation & Sleep + Stress & Mental Health leaves
hypotheses.claim: Wellness incumbents are losing revenue while challengers grow. A merge/garden self-care pet can reach at least 5% trial and at least 20% D7 at CPI of $2.5 or less. Falsified otherwise.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium-high: HHI 0.07-0.08, new-entrant share 4-10%; strong merge/garden fit.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Pet island grows when 3 micro-habits are done; merge decorations; light AI journaling; yearly subscription.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable ad ('merge to calm your pet') plus a fake-door subscription on a test build, US, $3k, 3 weeks. Pass: CPI ≤ $2.5, trial ≥ 5%, D7 ≥ 20%.
hypotheses.risks: Shrinking leaves, Finch owns the concept, mental-health policy, invisible web2app revenue.

verification.reasoning: The market numbers hold up, but they don't support the opportunity as framed. Combined top-100 revenue is $404.0M vs $441.9M (-8.6%). In Stress & Mental Health the challengers are not making up for the shrinking incumbents: entrants added +$9.3M across 29 apps (about $0.32M each), against both-period apps -$6.8M and exits -$5.2M. The apps that did grow are 2014-vintage Spanish affirmation and quote apps (I am +46%, Motivation +116%) and AI journals or chat apps, not gamified pets. The concept is owned outright: Finch is #1 with a 25% share of the top-100 ($28.9M, +3% YoY but H2/H1 -22%, last3m -13%, downloads -36%). So the category creator is already saturating. The closest new-entrant clone, Catzy: Self-Care Journey (2024-11, China), reached 3.36M downloads but only $0.51M of IAP revenue. That is about $0.15 per download, against Finch's $3.12, which shows a small team can win installs but not store revenue. Rank #50 in the niche earns only $0.41M a year. At the proposed US CPI of $2.5, an entrant needs Finch-level conversion just to break even. Low HHI (0.074–0.082) reflects a long tail of tiny apps, not an open door. The revenue_test is the fatal problem. A fake-door paywall measures trial-intent clicks, not paid conversion or trial-to-paid. The pass criteria (CPI, trial ≥5%, D7 ≥20%) contain no revenue metric at all. The test also skips the parts that make the concept hard to copy: a real StoreKit trial with ~7-day conversion, a refund/churn read, and the policy review a mental-health claim attracts. It could be repaired by running a real subscription with a 3-day trial on a live build and measuring paid conversion per install against CPI. As written, though, it cannot falsify a revenue hypothesis. The cited 'Personal Health & Fitness leaf top-5 incumbents -8% vs challengers +16%' adds nothing for this concept. That leaf's top-100 is +3.8%, and its growth comes from hardware or AI-coach apps (Hume Health +408%, Bevel +340%, Fitbit $74.4M), which a self-care pet would not capture.

hypotheses.title: Daily-ritual puzzle bundle (word + logic) on subscription
hypotheses.market: Word + Riddle game sub-genres; Brain Training Apps as the losing positioning (WW, US/GB)
hypotheses.claim: Word is shrinking ($251.2M -> $235.9M, downloads -19.6%) and brain-training apps collapse ($85.3M -> $58.5M), but the daily-ritual subscription bundle grows (NYT Games $52.4M -> $66.6M, RPD $9.92) while ad/IAP word apps shrink (Wordscapes -27%, Words With Friends -47%). A 'daily bundle' of the feed's micro-games (association grid, seat logic, cryptogram) with streaks and an archive beats a 'brain training' landing page on trial intent and converts a measurable share of visitors. Falsified if brain-training positioning converts equally or better, or trial starts miss the pre-set rate.

evidence.metric: Word revenue; NYT Games; Wordscapes; Words With Friends
NYT Games revenue, RPD, iOS share

hypotheses.accessibility: High build feasibility (reuses feed micro-games), low ceiling without a brand: Word top1 NYT Games 30.4%, new entrants 7.7%. Riddle is fragmented (76% new entrants) but tiny in IAP ($23M) and ad-monetized (ad_intensity_us 21.6).
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Three daily puzzles (association grid, seat logic, cryptogram) with streaks; free daily plus a subscription for archive and hints.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 2-week US Meta paid social to two landing pages (daily bundle vs brain training) with a fake-door subscription checkout, ~$2k each; compare CTR and trial intent.
hypotheses.risks: NYT brand and content moat; subscription churn without a habit loop; tiny IAP base; value is mostly ad revenue the data cannot see. Conflicts with the brain-training reboot hypothesis (apps analyst reads the brain-training collapse as incumbent-specific; this one reads it as demand moving to daily-ritual bundles). Measurement boundary: Sensor Tower store IAP + paid downloads only (App Store + Google Play); no ad revenue, web/D2C, third-party Android or mainland-China Android.

verification.reasoning: Every headline number reproduces exactly. Word is $251.23M -> $235.86M (-6.1%) with downloads -19.6% (niche_dynamics_game_sub_genre.csv). NYT Games is $52.39M -> $66.62M (+27.2%); 6.71M downloads gives RPD $9.92, and iOS share is 85.6% (leaders.csv). Brain Training top-100 is $85.34M -> $58.45M (-31.5%). Riddle is $11.72M -> $23.01M (+96%), with 76.0% new-entrant share and 1,049M downloads. The mechanism does not hold up, though. (1) The 'daily-ritual bundle grows' leg rests on one app. NYT Games has a 30.4% top1 share of Word, and its downloads fell 26% (9.11M -> 6.71M), so the gain is ARPU/price from an existing brand subscriber base, not growing demand for daily rituals. The NYTimes news app also grew +13.5% in the same period, which points to bundle pricing. (2) The brain-training 'collapse' is a single incumbent. Impulse fell $46.82M -> $21.69M, which is -$25.1M of the niche's -$26.9M drop (93%). That is not evidence that the 'brain training' positioning is losing. The tag is also unstable: total_count rose from 462 to 780, and the filter looks recently created. (3) Excluding NYT, Word falls 14.9% ($198.8M -> $169.2M). The only daily-style new entrants are small: Associations-Colorwood $1.4M, Cryptogram $1.1M, and NYT Crossplay is downloads-only. (4) Riddle's +96% comes entirely from new entrants (growth_decomp_entrants_share_of_abs_delta 1.10, both -0.06) on a sub-$50M base. Its top names are match/seat-logic games (Connect Master $5.8M, That's My Seat $3.9M) whose That's My Seat series is already fading (s_rev_h2_h1 -35%, last3m -55%). Riddle is also ad-monetized (ad_intensity_us 21.6, unranked because prior < $20M). The test design (landing-page A/B) is fine as a hypothesis, but the market data supports only 'NYT's moat monetizes harder', not 'demand moves to daily bundles'.

verification.key_caveat: Both trend legs come down to one app each. The 'daily-bundle growth' is NYT Games alone (30% of Word, downloads -26%, so growth is brand ARPU, not new users). The 'brain-training collapse' is 93% Impulse. Neither shows category-level demand moving away from brain-training positioning. All figures are Sensor Tower App Store + Google Play IAP only: they exclude ad revenue (which dominates Riddle) and NYT web subscriptions.

verification.reasoning: The data shows that the "daily-ritual subscription" money sits with brands. A small studio does not have a way in. In Word, the top-100 lost 7.6% ($237.3M to $219.3M). NYT Games alone holds 30.4% of it, and the top 3 hold 47.9%. New entrants hold only 7.7%, and none of them is a subscription daily bundle: the five biggest (Bubble Word Jam, Crossword Go!, Associations - Colorwood and others) are IAP/ad progression games. The only other subscription-style bundle in the top 25 is The Telegraph, a news app ($7.0M). Take NYT out and Word fell 17.4% ($184.9M to $152.7M). NYT's +27% came while its downloads dropped 26%, which is consistent with price or bundle effects of an existing NYT subscriber base, not with open demand. The brain-training "collapse" is one company: Impulse went from $46.8M to $21.7M, which is 93% of the $26.9M decline. Without Impulse the category moved only -4.6% ($38.5M to $36.8M). So brain training is a weak control in the A/B test, not proof that demand moved to daily bundles. The micro-games named in the prototype are already fading as IAP products. That's My Seat has H2/H1 -35% and last-3-month YoY -55%. Cryptogram: Word Logic Puzzles is down 53%. Riddle doubled only through new titles ($12.1M from entrants, while incumbents fell $0.7M), and earns $0.022 per download. Its US ad intensity is 21.6, so most of its value is ad revenue that store IAP data cannot see. Where non-brand association games do make IAP money, it is the IAP progression format (Solitaire Associations Journey $43.8M, released 2025-08, H2/H1 +155%), not a subscription. The proposed test fails on its own terms. A fake-door checkout behind two Meta landing pages measures CTR and stated trial intent, not paid conversion or retention, and subscription value depends on retention. hypotheses.title: Turkish Okey is closed to multiplayer entrants; only a solo puzzle variant might enter
hypotheses.market: Turkey
hypotheses.claim: No multiplayer Okey entrant gets traction (WW entrants cap at $0.3M), but a single-player Okey-tile puzzle reaches TR playable-ad CTR >= the TR benchmark for Match Swap creatives.

evidence.value: 101 Okey Plus $15.1M (US-HQ), 101 Okey Yalla $6.9M (AE), Soho $5.4M (CN); local 10%

hypotheses.accessibility: Low for multiplayer clones (91% top-10, under 1% entrants). Moderate for a solo puzzle reinterpretation, which sidesteps liquidity.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Level-based Okey or rummy-meld puzzle (clear the rack in N moves), Turkish themes, rewarded ads plus boosters.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad CTR/CPI test in TR (2 weeks, $1.5k) against a Match Swap control creative.
hypotheses.risks: Okey players may want social play, not puzzles. TRY FX. Turkey is home to the strongest casual publishers.

verification.reasoning:
The data supports the negative half of the claim: multiplayer Okey is closed to new entrants. WW Okey earned $51.4M, up 21.0% YoY. Top-10 share is 91.3% and the top-1 app alone takes 32.0%. New entrants hold 0.79% ($0.41M) and the largest is 101 OKEY Mİ&Tavla at $0.3M. Incumbents produced 104.5% of the growth, while entrants into the top 100 produced 4.1%. Every top-5 incumbent grew 13-27%.

The opportunity half has no support in the data. A solo Okey-tile puzzle is not the demand being measured. That demand is mostly live, voice/social, chip-based table play from US/AE/CN publishers: TR leaders Okey Plus $15.1M, Yalla $6.9M, Soho $5.4M. The data room contains no single-player Okey title showing revenue. A solo variant would actually compete in TR Match Swap ($45.8M, but downloads -10.1%) against Royal Match ($13.8M), made by a top Turkish publisher.

The decisive problem is the test. A 2-week, $1.5k CTR/CPI comparison against a Match Swap creative measures clicks and install cost, not revenue. It cannot show whether an Okey player pays for boosters or watches rewarded ads, and the hypothesis's own success criterion ("CTR >= benchmark") is a click metric. The TR USD revenue growth also partly reflects lira inflation and price pass-through, and Okey chip economies sit close to Turkey's gambling and social-casino store policies. Because the niche's IAP data is all multiplayer, it gives no evidence either for or against ad-monetized solo demand.

hypotheses.prototype_idea: French Tarot vs 3 AI players with hints, daily deals and a coach mode; subscription and no-ads IAP.
hypotheses.revenue_test: FR soft launch, 4 weeks: CPI, D7, subscription trial conversion. Or a fake-door subscription page from FR Meta ads.
hypotheses.risks: Shrinking installs. Incumbents own multiplayer liquidity. Small absolute ceiling (about $26M market).

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers check out (country_niche_dynamics.csv): FR Tabletop Cards went from $23.0M to $26.4M (+14.7%) with downloads -23.9%, and DE went from $20.8M to $23.1M (+11.3%) with downloads -25.5%. Worldwide the niche is flat at +3.1% and its H2/H1 momentum is -0.2%. The word 'fragmented' does not hold, though. The worldwide HHI of 0.067 comes from a global mix of Chinese, Arab and US titles. Inside France, six apps in the country top-300 (Belote.com $8.23M, Tarot Classique $5.04M, Rummy Fun & Friends $4.93M, Fun Bridge $2.38M, UNO $1.23M, Belote & Coinche $1.20M) earn $23.0M, or 87% of the FR niche. FR growth is also incumbent-led: Tarot Classique alone added +$1.68M of the +$3.38M FR delta (50%). In DE, Rummy Fun & Friends added +$2.59M, which is more than the whole niche delta of +$2.34M, so the rest of the DE niche shrank. Every winner is a multiplayer or 'en ligne'/'Multijoueur'/'Live' liquidity app, and the three FR leaders are all German-published. A single-player-vs-AI app is not the format that is earning. The 2024 entrant example cuts both ways: Tarot Classique grew revenue +53% while its downloads halved (945k to 459k worldwide). That is a retained, monetizing multiplayer base, not evidence that a new title can buy its way in. The total ceiling is small, about $26M in FR, and the hypothesis would have to take share from a ~$5M tarot leader inside a shrinking install pool. The prototype itself is buildable in 4 weeks. The test only partly measures revenue. D7 trial starts show up inside the window, but trial-to-paid conversion and churn for an older FR audience mostly land after week 4. The fake-door variant measures clicks, not payments. Ad-monetized demand matters less here: US ad_intensity is 1.48 (rank 32) and the niche's iOS impression share fell -1.02pp, so IAP data probably does not hide a large ad-funded market. Regulatory risk is low as long as there are no cash or sweepstakes mechanics and no real-money tarot or belote.

hypotheses.title: GB daily word puzzles grow against a shrinking WW Word niche
hypotheses.market: United Kingdom
hypotheses.claim: A daily-puzzle bundle (word plus logic plus mini-crossword) fake-door subscription page gets >= 4% trial intent from GB paid social at CPC <= £0.60.

evidence.value: NYT Games $6.7M, The Telegraph $5.6M; local share 46%

hypotheses.accessibility: Medium-low. Brand-led by newspapers; a small studio competes on format innovation, not brand. Cheap to prototype.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Daily 3-puzzle pack with streaks and a friend leaderboard; subscription with a free daily tier.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Fake-door landing page plus Meta and TikTok ads in GB, 2 weeks, about £1.5k: CTR, signup and trial-intent rate.
hypotheses.risks: NYT and Telegraph brand moat. Word UA is ad-heavy (US ad-intensity rank 13). Growth may be brand subscription bundles, not standalone games. Local cut of the daily-ritual puzzle bundle hypothesis.

verification.reasoning: The GB Word growth comes almost entirely from two newspaper brands. GB Word revenue rose by +$3.22M ($20.96M to $24.19M, country_niche_dynamics.csv). Over the same window NYT Games grew $4.07M to $6.71M (+$2.64M) and The Telegraph grew $4.93M to $5.62M (+$0.69M), together +$3.33M (country_leaders.csv, GB revenue order). So the rest of GB Word was flat to slightly down: $11.96M to $11.86M (-0.9%). The 'growth' is subscription bundles that pair a news app with puzzles, not demand a standalone game can reach. The Telegraph is also a news app carrying the Word tag, so part of the niche is a taxonomy artifact. Only 2 Word apps reach GB's top-300 by revenue, and both are legacy brands released in 2009-2010. Worldwide, Word is declining: revenue -6.1%, downloads -19.6%. The top-100's change splits into -$32.1M from apps present in both years and +$19.2M from entrants. New entrants hold 7.7% of top-100 revenue, but the ones that worked are mechanic hybrids such as Bubble Word Jam ($4.4M) and Associations - Colorwood ($1.4M), not daily-bundle subscriptions. The niche is concentrated: NYT alone is 30.4% of the top-100 and the top-3 hold 47.9%. The proposed test is a fake-door page measuring CTR, sign-ups and 'trial intent' with no payment step, so it measures clicks, not revenue. Nothing in the data supports the 4% intent or £0.60 CPC thresholds. Word is also ad-funded (US ad-intensity rank 13, Android impression share 4.16%), and that ad revenue is invisible in this IAP data. A free-tier daily puzzle would likely earn mostly from ads, which the test cannot see either.

Part of the in-app growth may be a shift between payment channels rather than new demand. 'Local share 46%' just means the Telegraph is about 46% of the two GB Word apps in the top-300.

The data does back one point: brand-led daily-puzzle subscriptions are growing in GB. It does not show a growing standalone word-game niche that a small studio could enter. The tested claim (trial intent of at least 4% at CPC of £0.60 or less) cannot be checked against these CSVs at all.

hypotheses.title: Brain-training reboot on puzzle-game mechanics
hypotheses.market: Brain Training Apps leaf
hypotheses.claim: The brain-training collapse is specific to the incumbents. A puzzle-mechanic daily workout can get CPI of $2 or less and at least 4% trial. Falsified if CPI is over $3 or trial under 3% (demand has moved to games).

evidence.value: Matiks 7.1M dl; IQ Masters $8.5M tagged Education & Training

hypotheses.accessibility: High (weak incumbents, HHI 0.23) but the market is small and shrinking; highest mechanic fit.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: 5 daily puzzle drills (sort, merge-math, pattern) with a brain-age score and weekly report; focus-training subscription with a free daily drill.
hypotheses.revenue_test: 2-week build reusing existing mechanics; AppLovin/Unity playable ads, US, $3k. Pass: CPI ≤ $2, trial ≥ 4%, D7 ≥ 20%.
hypotheses.risks: Declining category, health claims, limited upside. Conflicts with the daily-ritual bundle hypothesis, which reads the brain-training decline as demand moving to daily bundles rather than incumbent weakness.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce exactly. In niche_leaders_full_app_iq_category.csv (Brain Training Apps, status complete), the top 100 earned $58.45M vs $85.34M (-31.5%), with HHI 0.228. Recomputing from niche_top_apps.csv, the prior-period top 5 fell 36.8% ($77.81M to $49.20M) and the other 67 apps present in both periods rose 17.1% ($7.51M to $8.79M). The decline is not reclassification: in the growth decomposition, apps present in both periods account for -$27.33M, entrants for only +$0.47M and exits for -$0.03M. But it is a single-app artifact rather than a story about incumbents as a group. Impulse alone fell $46.82M to $21.69M, which is -$25.14M, or about 93% of the niche's -$26.89M. Without Impulse the top 100 went from $38.52M to $36.77M, only -4.6% (flat). The other four incumbents fell just 11.2% ($30.99M to $27.51M). The +17% for challengers adds up to only +$1.28M on a $7.5M base, and BrainHQ (a 2012 app) supplies about half of it. The challengers cited as proof of demand barely earn anything in the stores. Matiks made $210 of in-app revenue on 7.11M downloads, and Brainova made $21.8K on 3.6M downloads. So their demand is either ad-monetized, which this IAP-only data cannot see, or not monetized at all. Either way it is not evidence that a subscription can earn. IQ Masters (tagged Education & Training) is weakening too: H2/H1 -26%, last-3-month YoY -39%, downloads down 53% (leaders.csv). Elevate's H2/H1 of -40% shows the #2 player is speeding up its decline. The falsification test (CPI ≤ $2, trial ≥ 4%) cannot be checked with this data room at all, because no CPI or conversion data exists. The tag's app count rising from 462 to 780 apps also suggests the tag was recently broadened.

verification.key_caveat: The niche's "-32% collapse" is almost entirely one app: Impulse fell $25.1M, about 93% of the decline. Without it the brain-training top 100 is flat (-4.6%) on a ~$37M base. The download-heavy challengers (Matiks 7.1M downloads and $210 IAP; Brainova 3.6M downloads and $22K) show almost no in-store revenue, which the IAP-only data cannot explain. The CPI and trial thresholds are untestable with Sensor Tower data.

verification.reasoning: The decline itself checks out: Brain Training top-100 revenue was $58.45M vs $85.34M (-31.5%). It is not specific to the incumbents, though, and the accessibility case is overstated. HHI 0.228 with top3 share 0.73 and top10 share 0.95 is a concentrated niche, not one with weak incumbents. Challengers outside the top 5 did grow (+23% for the same app IDs), but only from $7.51M to $9.26M, a gain of about +$1.75M against a -$28.6M loss for the top 5. All 31 new entrants together earn $1.70M (2.9% of the top 100), and the 28 entrants into the top 100 earn $0.47M. The entrants that won downloads did not earn IAP revenue: Matiks had 7.1M downloads and about $0.0 IAP, Brainova 3.6M downloads and $0.02M. That points to ad-monetized or free demand that store IAP data cannot see. It does not show a subscription market open to a new entrant. The "demand moved to games" alternative also fails in the data: brain-puzzle games are declining too (Brain Test -7% yoy, Brain Out -33%, Brain Test All-Star -42%). IQ Masters, filed under Education & Training, is +3% yoy but -26% H2/H1 and -39% over the last three months. So the whole cognitive-puzzle pool is shrinking, not just the incumbents. The weakest part of the test is what it measures. CPI and a 4% trial-start rate are pre-revenue metrics. Two weeks and $3k at a $2 CPI buys about 1,500 installs and about 60 trials, so no trial-to-paid conversion or renewal can be observed. AppLovin/Unity game-network playable traffic also skews toward players who never pay for a subscription. A 2-week build is feasible for a puzzle studio, and BrainGain (launched 2024-04, $2.1M, +17%) shows a small entrant can reach seven figures. The realistic ceiling is a low single-digit $M slice of a niche that is shrinking more than 30% a year. The test must add a hard paid-conversion gate, and health claims bring FTC risk (precedent: Lumosity's 2016 settlement).

verification.key_caveat: The proposed test measures CPI and trial starts, not revenue. Brain-training entrants that won downloads (Matiks 7.1M, Brainova 3.6M) earned about $0 IAP, and Sensor Tower data cannot see ad revenue. A pass on this test therefore says nothing about subscription revenue in a niche whose top 100 fell 31.5% and where new entrants hold 2.9% of revenue.

hypotheses.title: Gulf card games (SA, AE): Jackaroo King proved a 2024 entrant can break through
hypotheses.market: Saudi Arabia and UAE
hypotheses.claim: An Arabic-first Jackaroo or Baloot variant with bots and friend rooms hits CPI <= $1.50 in SA/AE and keeps D7 >= 20%.
hypotheses.accessibility: Medium. Fragmented with a recent entrant success, but it needs multiplayer liquidity and Arabic social UX. SA games local-publisher share is only 2.4%.
hypotheses.prototype_idea: Jackaroo or Baloot with AI bots, voice-free quick chat, friend rooms and Ramadan events.
hypotheses.revenue_test: Playable-ad CPI test in SA+AE (2 weeks, $3k), then a 3-week SA soft launch measuring D7 and ARPDAU.
hypotheses.risks: Social games need liquidity. Modest growth. Payment and cultural localization.

verification.reasoning: The numbers check out, but they describe a mature, concentrated niche, not a growing one. SA Tabletop Cards grew from $12.79M to $14.03M (+9.7%, so just under the +10% "growing" threshold). SA downloads fell 20.9%, and AE Tabletop Cards is flat at $5.80M (-0.8%, downloads -9.4%). Five apps take about 92% of SA niche revenue: Kammelna $6.15M, Jackaroo King $3.49M, Jawaker $1.85M, Yalla Baloot $0.98M and ملك الورق $0.49M, together $12.96M of $14.03M. That contradicts "fragmented". The Jackaroo King breakthrough is a 2024-25 event already counted in the prior window. It came with heavy acquisition: 12.5M WW downloads in its first year, then 4.9M (-61%). Its revenue is now flattening (H2/H1 -2.3%, last3m YoY -7%), and its publisher is a Singapore company, not a small local team. So it proves that a funded entrant could break through two years ago, not that the window is open now. The other Jackaroo app, Mdagsh (China), fell from $2.05M to $1.50M in SA, which shows the second slot in the same game is shrinking. The proposed test does not measure revenue. Stage 1 measures playable-ad CPI and stage 2 measures D7, which are click and retention proxies. A 3-week ARPDAU read on a liquidity-dependent multiplayer card game, with real players diluted by bots, will be noisy and too small to project LTV. Building a real-time Arabic multiplayer game with friend rooms in 4 weeks is also a stretch for a puzzle/merge studio. Ramadan events cannot be tested inside that window (Ramadan 2027 starts around Feb 2027). Ad-monetized demand is not the main blind spot here: Tabletop Cards ad_intensity_us=1.48 (rank 32). Most of the regional money sits in voice-chat/gifting Board apps (Yalla Ludo, TopTop, سوا بلاي), which IAP data does capture, and the "voice-free" design leaves that money out on purpose.

About 92% of SA revenue sits in five apps, and the 2024 Jackaroo King breakthrough was backed by about 12.5M first-year downloads of paid acquisition. The proposed CPI/D7 test measures clicks and retention, not revenue, and a 3-week soft launch cannot show ARPDAU for a liquidity-dependent multiplayer game.

verification.reasoning: The headline numbers reproduce. SA Tabletop Cards is $12.79M -> $14.03M (+9.7%) with H2/H1 +13.0% (country_niche_dynamics.csv). Note that the file classes this as rev_class=flat, not growing, and the niche's SA downloads fell 21% (7.22M -> 5.71M). Jackaroo King is SA $3.49M, AE $2.45M and WW $10.25M; Kammelna SA is $6.15M (+13%); SA games local-publisher share comes out at 2.4%; and the revenue index I recompute is 8.50 against the claimed 8.85. The 'niche growth', however, is two apps. In SA, Kammelna added +$0.73M and Jackaroo King +$0.68M, while Jawaker fell -$0.33M (country_leaders.csv). It is also a taxonomy artifact. Jackaroo and Baloot titles are spread across three tags: Tabletop Cards, Casino Cards (Mdagsh Jackaroo, which fell in SA from $2.05M to $1.50M, -27%; also the Baloot apps) and Board (جلسة بلوت, Jackaroo Club and Jackaroo Star). SA Tabletop Cards plus Casino Cards went from $22.46M to $21.68M (-3.5%), and the same pair within SA top-300 apps went from $21.32M to $20.44M (-4.2%). So the Gulf card-game pool is flat to shrinking, and revenue is shifting between buckets rather than growing. The 'entrant broke through' story also happened mostly in the prior window. Jackaroo King's WW downloads fell 61% (12.52M -> 4.92M), its SA downloads 59% (3.17M -> 1.29M) and its AE downloads 49%. Its revenue series shows H2/H1 -2.3% and last-3-months YoY -7.0%, with a peak in 2026-03 (the Ramadan window). Its +24% revenue YoY comes from monetizing a shrinking launch cohort, not from ongoing breakout. AE Tabletop Cards is flat ($5.85M -> $5.80M, -0.8%; downloads -9%), and SA Board is declining (-11.8%). The claim's CPI <= $1.50 and D7 >= 20% targets cannot be checked at all from this data. Store revenue covers IAP only, so web and voice-room payments and ad revenue in these social games are invisible to it.
